label: दोहा
hi: श्रीगुरु चरन सरोज रज निज मनु मुकुरु सुधारि।
बरनउँ रघुबर बिमल जसु जो दायकु फल चारि॥
en: Shreeguru charan saroj raj nij manu mukuru sudhaari |
Baranaun raghubar bimal jasu jo daayaku phal chaari ||
mean: Cleansing the mirror of my mind with the dust of my Guru's lotus feet, I sing the pure glory of Shri Ram, which bestows the four fruits of life.

label: दोहा
hi: बल बुधि बिद्या देहु मोहिं हरहु कलेस बिकार॥
en: Bal budhi bidyaa dehu mohin harahu kales bikaar ||
mean: Knowing myself to be lacking in wisdom, I remember Hanuman, son of the Wind. Grant me strength, intelligence and knowledge, and remove my troubles and faults.

label: चौपाई 1
mean: Victory to Hanuman, ocean of wisdom and virtue. Victory to the lord of monkeys, who lights up the three worlds.

label: चौपाई 2
mean: You are Ram's messenger, the abode of matchless strength, known as Anjani's son and the son of the Wind.

label: चौपाई 3
mean: Great hero, mighty and with a body strong as a thunderbolt, you drive away bad thinking and stay with those of good mind.

label: चौपाई 4
mean: Your complexion is golden and your dress is fine; you wear earrings and your hair is curly.

label: चौपाई 5
mean: In your hands shine the thunderbolt and the flag, and a sacred thread of munj grass adorns your shoulder.

label: चौपाई 6
mean: You are the son of Shankar and the joy of Kesari; your radiance and glory are honoured by the whole world.

label: चौपाई 7
mean: Learned, virtuous and very clever, you are always eager to do Ram's work.

label: चौपाई 8
mean: You delight in hearing the Lord's deeds; Ram, Lakshman and Sita live in your heart.

label: चौपाई 9
mean: Taking a tiny form you appeared before Sita, and taking a fearsome form you burned Lanka.

label: चौपाई 10
mean: In a mighty form you destroyed the demons and completed Shri Ram's tasks.

label: चौपाई 11
mean: You brought the Sanjivani herb and revived Lakshman; Shri Ram embraced you with joy.

label: चौपाई 12
hi: तुम मम प्रिय भरतहि सम भाई॥
en: Tum mam priy bharatahi sam bhaaee ||
mean: Ram praised you greatly and said, 'You are as dear to me as my brother Bharat.'

label: चौपाई 13
mean: 'May the thousand-headed Shesh sing your glory,' said the Lord, and held you to his heart.

label: चौपाई 14
mean: Sanak and the sages, Brahma and the gods, Narad, Saraswati and Shesh the king of serpents...

label: चौपाई 15
hi: कबि कोबिद कहि सके कहाँ ते॥
en: Kabi kobid kahi sake kahaan te ||
mean: ...Yama, Kubera and the guardians of the directions, poets and scholars - none can fully describe your glory.

label: चौपाई 16
mean: You did Sugriv a great favour: you brought him to Ram and he regained his kingdom.

label: चौपाई 17
mean: Vibhishan followed your counsel and became king of Lanka, as the whole world knows.

label: चौपाई 18
mean: The sun, thousands of yojans away, you swallowed, thinking it a sweet fruit.

label: चौपाई 19
mean: Holding the Lord's ring in your mouth you leapt across the ocean - no wonder in that.

label: चौपाई 20
mean: Every difficult task in the world becomes easy by your grace.

label: चौपाई 21
mean: You are the guard at Ram's door; no one enters without your permission.

label: चौपाई 22
hi: तुम रच्छक काहू को डर ना॥
en: Tum rachchhak kaahoo ko dar naa ||
mean: One who takes refuge in you finds every joy; with you as protector there is nothing to fear.

label: चौपाई 23
mean: Only you can contain your own might; the three worlds tremble at your roar.

label: चौपाई 24
mean: Ghosts and evil spirits do not come near when one calls out the name of Mahavir.

label: चौपाई 25
mean: Disease is destroyed and all pain removed by constantly chanting the name of brave Hanuman.

label: चौपाई 26
hi: मन क्रम बचन ध्यान जो लावै॥
en: Man kram bachan dhyaan jo laavai ||
mean: Hanuman frees from trouble those who fix their thought, deed and word on him.

label: चौपाई 27
hi: तिन के काज सकल तुम साजा॥
en: Tin ke kaaj sakal tum saajaa ||
mean: Ram, the ascetic king, is above all, and you carry out all his tasks.

label: चौपाई 28
mean: Whoever brings any wish to you receives the boundless fruit of life.

label: चौपाई 29
mean: Your glory shines through all four ages and lights up the world.

label: चौपाई 30
mean: You are the protector of saints and sages, destroyer of demons, and beloved of Ram.

label: चौपाई 31
hi: अष्ट सिद्धि नौ निधि के दाता।
en: Asht siddhi nau nidhi ke daataa |
mean: You grant the eight siddhis and nine treasures - a boon given to you by Mother Janaki.

label: चौपाई 32
mean: You hold the elixir of devotion to Ram; may you always remain his servant.

label: चौपाई 33
mean: Through devotion to you one reaches Ram and forgets the sorrows of many lifetimes.

label: चौपाई 34
mean: At the end one goes to Ram's abode, and if born again is known as a devotee of Hari.

label: चौपाई 35
mean: Even without holding other gods in mind, serving Hanuman brings every happiness.

label: चौपाई 36
mean: Troubles are cut away and all pain ends for one who remembers mighty Hanuman.

label: चौपाई 37
mean: Hail, hail, hail Lord Hanuman! Be gracious to me as a Guru is.

label: चौपाई 38
hi: जो सत बार पाठ कर कोई।
en: Jo sat baar paath kar koee |
mean: Whoever recites this a hundred times is freed from bondage and finds great joy.

label: चौपाई 39
mean: Whoever reads this Hanuman Chalisa gains success; Lord Shiva is witness.

label: चौपाई 40
mean: Tulsidas is forever Hari's servant; Lord, make your home in my heart.

label: दोहा
hi: पवनतनय संकट हरन मंगल मूरति रूप।
राम लखन सीता सहित हृदय बसहु सुर भूप॥
en: Pavanatanay sankat haran mangal moorati roop |
Raam lakhan seetaa sahit hriday basahu sur bhoop ||
mean: Son of the Wind, remover of troubles, embodiment of blessings - dwell in my heart along with Ram, Lakshman and Sita, O king of gods.

label: श्लोक 1
mean: I bow to Ram, lord of the universe: peaceful, eternal, beyond measure, sinless, giver of liberation, served by Brahma, Shiva and Shesh, known through the Vedanta, who took human form - the jewel among kings, ocean of compassion.

label: श्लोक 2
mean: O Raghupati, I truly have no other desire in my heart - you know every heart. Grant me complete devotion, and free my mind from desire and other faults.

label: श्लोक 3
mean: I bow to Hanuman, son of the Wind: abode of matchless strength, with a body bright as a golden mountain, fire to the forest of demons, foremost of the wise, treasure of virtues, lord of the monkeys and beloved devotee of Ram.
Jambavan's encouraging words pleased Hanuman's heart deeply.

hi: तब लगि मोहि परिखेहु तुम्ह भाई।
सहि दुख कंद मूल फल खाई॥
en: Tab lagi mohi parikhehu tumh bhaaee |
Sahi dukh kand mool phal khaaee ||
mean: He said, 'Brothers, wait for me here, enduring hardship and living on roots and fruits...'
'...until I return having seen Sita. The task will succeed, and I feel great joy.'

hi: यह कहि नाइ सबन्हि कहुँ माथा।
en: Yah kahi naai sabanhi kahun maathaa |
mean: Saying this and bowing his head to all, he set off joyfully, holding Ram in his heart.
On the seashore stood a beautiful mountain; he playfully leapt up onto it.
Remembering Ram again and again, the Wind's son sprang with great force.
The mountain on which he pressed his feet sank at once into the netherworld.
Like Ram's unfailing arrow, Hanuman sped through the sky.
The ocean, knowing him to be Ram's messenger, told Mount Mainak: 'Rise and relieve his weariness.'

label: दोहा 1
hi: हनूमान तेहि परसा कर पुनि कीन्ह प्रनाम।
राम काजु कीन्हें बिनु मोहि कहाँ बिश्राम॥
en: Hanoomaan tehi parasaa kar puni keenh pranaam |
Raam kaaju keenhen binu mohi kahaan bishraam ||
mean: Hanuman touched the mountain with his hand and bowed, saying, 'How can I rest until Ram's work is done?'
The gods saw the Wind's son going and wished to test his strength and wisdom.
They sent Surasa, mother of serpents, who came and spoke to him.
'Today the gods have given me my meal.' Hearing this, Hanuman replied:

hi: राम काजु करि फिरि मैं आवौं।
en: Raam kaaju kari phiri main aavaun |
mean: 'Let me do Ram's work and return, and give the Lord news of Sita...'

hi: सत्य कहउँ मोहि जान दे माई॥
en: Saty kahaun mohi jaan de maaee ||
mean: '...then I will come and enter your mouth. I speak the truth, mother - let me go.'
When she would not let him go by any means, Hanuman said, 'Then swallow me.'
She opened her mouth a yojan wide; Hanuman made his body twice as large.
She made her mouth sixteen yojans; at once he became thirty-two.
However wide Surasa opened her mouth, the monkey showed a form twice as large.
When she made her mouth a hundred yojans, he took a very tiny form.
He entered her mouth, came out again, bowed his head and asked leave to go.

hi: बुधि बल मरमु तोर मै पावा॥
en: Budhi bal maramu tor mai paavaa ||
mean: She said, 'I have tested the strength and wisdom the gods sent me to test.'

label: दोहा 2
hi: राम काजु सबु करिहहु तुम्ह बल बुद्धि निधान।
आसिष देह गई सो हरषि चलेउ हनुमान॥
en: Raam kaaju sabu karihahu tumh bal buddhi nidhaan |
Aasish deh gaee so harashi chaleu hanumaan ||
mean: 'You will accomplish all of Ram's work, treasure of strength and wisdom.' Blessing him, she left, and Hanuman went on joyfully.

hi: करि माया नभु के खग गहई॥
en: Kari maayaa nabhu ke khag gahaee ||
mean: A demoness lived in the sea who, by magic, caught birds flying in the sky.
When creatures flew overhead, she watched their reflections in the water...

hi: गहइ छाहँ सक सो न उड़ाई।
en: Gahai chhaahan sak so na udaaee |
mean: ...and by seizing the shadow held them so they could not fly; thus she fed on sky-farers.
She tried the same trick on Hanuman, but he saw through her deceit at once.
Killing her, the brave and steady Hanuman crossed to the far shore.
There he saw the beauty of the forest, with bees humming after honey.

hi: खग मृग बृंद देखि मन भाए॥
en: Khag mrig brind dekhi man bhaae ||
mean: Trees of many kinds with fruit and flowers, and flocks of birds and deer, pleased his heart.

hi: ता पर धाइ चढेउ भय त्यागें॥
en: Taa par dhaai chadheu bhay tyaagen ||
mean: Seeing a huge mountain ahead, he ran up it fearlessly.

hi: उमा न कछु कपि कै अधिकाई।
en: Umaa na kachhu kapi kai adhikaaee |
mean: (Shiva says:) Uma, there is nothing special in the monkey himself; it is the Lord's glory, which devours even Death.

hi: गिरि पर चढि लंका तेहिं देखी।
कहि न जाइ अति दुर्ग बिसेषी॥
en: Giri par chadhi lankaa tehin dekhee |
Kahi na jaai ati durg biseshee ||
mean: From the mountain top he saw Lanka - a fortress beyond description.
Very high, with the ocean on all sides, its golden walls shone brilliantly.

label: छंद 1
hi: कनक कोट बिचित्र मनि कृत सुंदरायतना घना।
चउहट्ट हट्ट सुबट्ट बीथीं चारु पुर बहु बिधि बना॥
गज बाजि खच्चर निकर पदचर रथ बरूथिन्ह को गनै॥
बहुरूप निसिचर जूथ अतिबल सेन बरनत नहिं बनै॥
en: Kanak kot bichitr mani krit sundaraayatanaa ghanaa |
Chauhatt hatt subatt beetheen chaaru pur bahu bidhi banaa ||
Gaj baaji khachchar nikar padachar rath baroothinh ko ganai ||
Bahuroop nisichar jooth atibal sen baranat nahin banai ||
mean: Golden ramparts studded with gems, many fine buildings, crossroads, markets, wide streets - a beautifully built city. Who could count its elephants, horses, mules, foot soldiers and chariots, or describe its mighty demon armies of many forms?

label: छंद 2
hi: बन बाग उपबन बाटिका सर कूप बापीं सोहहीं।
नर नाग सुर गंधर्ब कन्या रूप मुनि मन मोहहीं॥
कहुँ माल देह बिसाल सैल समान अतिबल गर्जहीं।
नाना अखारेन्ह भिरहिं बहु बिधि एक एकन्ह तर्जहीं॥
en: Ban baag upaban baatikaa sar koop baapeen sohaheen |
Nar naag sur gandharb kanyaa roop muni man mohaheen ||
Kahun maal deh bisaal sail samaan atibal garjaheen |
Naanaa akhaarenh bhirahin bahu bidhi ek ekanh tarjaheen ||
mean: Forests, gardens, groves, ponds, wells and step-wells adorned it; daughters of men, nagas, gods and gandharvas enchanted even sages. Wrestlers huge as mountains roared and grappled in many arenas.

label: छंद 3
hi: करि जतन भट कोटिन्ह बिकट तन नगर चहुँ दिसि रच्छहीं।
कहुँ महिष मानषु धेनु खर अज खल निसाचर भच्छहीं॥
एहि लागि तुलसीदास इन्ह की कथा कछु एक है कही।
रघुबीर सर तीरथ सरीरन्हि त्यागि गति पैहहिं सही॥
en: Kari jatan bhat kotinh bikat tan nagar chahun disi rachchhaheen |
Kahun mahish maanashu dhenu khar aj khal nisaachar bhachchhaheen ||
Ehi laagi tulaseedaas inh kee kathaa kachhu ek hai kahee |
Raghubeer sar teerath sareeranhi tyaagi gati paihahin sahee ||
mean: Millions of fierce warriors guarded the city on all sides, devouring buffaloes, men, cows, donkeys and goats. Tulsidas tells a little of them because, dying by Ram's arrows as at a sacred place, they will surely attain liberation.

label: दोहा 3
hi: पुर रखवारे देखि बहु कपि मन कीन्ह बिचार।
अति लघु रूप धरौं निसि नगर करौं पइसार॥
en: Pur rakhavaare dekhi bahu kapi man keenh bichaar |
Ati laghu roop dharaun nisi nagar karaun paisaar ||
mean: Seeing the many guards, Hanuman decided: 'I will take a tiny form and enter the city at night.'
Taking a form as small as a mosquito and remembering the Lord, he went toward Lanka.
A demoness named Lankini (guarding the city) said, 'You dare go past me?'
'Fool, don't you know my secret? Every thief here is my food.'
The great monkey struck her with one blow of his fist; vomiting blood, she fell to the ground.
Recovering, Lankini rose and, joining her palms, spoke humbly in fear:
'When Brahma gave Ravan his boon, he gave me a sign as he left:'

hi: बिकल होसि तैं कपि कें मारे।
en: Bikal hosi tain kapi ken maare |
mean: 'When a monkey's blow makes you reel, know that the demons' destruction is near.'
'Dear one, my merits are great indeed, for I have seen Ram's messenger with my own eyes.'

label: दोहा 4
hi: तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख धरिअ तुला एक अंग।
तूल न ताहि सकल मिलि जो सुख लव सतसंग॥
en: Taat svarg apabarg sukh dharia tulaa ek ang |
Tool na taahi sakal mili jo sukh lav satasang ||
mean: 'If heaven and liberation were placed on one side of a scale, together they would not equal a moment's joy of holy company.'
'Enter the city and do all your work, keeping the King of Kosal in your heart.'
For such a one, poison becomes nectar and enemies become friends; the ocean shrinks to a hoof-print and fire turns cool.
Mount Sumeru becomes like a speck of dust for one on whom Ram looks with grace.
Hanuman took a very small form and entered the city, remembering the Lord.
He searched every palace and saw countless warriors everywhere.

hi: अति बिचित्र कहि जात सो नाहीं॥
en: Ati bichitr kahi jaat so naaheen ||
mean: He went into Ravan's palace, which was wonderful beyond words.
He saw Ravan asleep, but Sita was not in that palace.
Then he saw a lovely house, with a separate temple to Hari built there.

label: दोहा 5
hi: रामायुध अंकित गृह सोभा बरनि न जाइ।
नव तुलसिका बृंद तहँ देखि हरषि कपिराइ॥
en: Raamaayudh ankit grih sobhaa barani na jaai |
Nav tulasikaa brind tahan dekhi harashi kapiraai ||
mean: The house was marked with Ram's weapons, its beauty indescribable; seeing fresh tulsi plants there, Hanuman rejoiced.
'Lanka is home to hordes of demons - how can a good person live here?'

hi: मन महुँ तरक करै कपि लागा।
en: Man mahun tarak karai kapi laagaa |
mean: As Hanuman pondered this, Vibhishan woke up.
He chanted 'Ram, Ram'; Hanuman rejoiced, recognising a good soul.

hi: साधु ते होइ न कारज हानी॥
en: Saadhu te hoi na kaaraj haanee ||
mean: 'I will make myself known to him; no harm comes to one's work from a saintly person.'
Taking the form of a Brahmin, he called out; hearing him, Vibhishan came out.
Bowing, he asked after his welfare: 'Brahmin, tell me who you are.'

hi: की तुम्ह हरि दासन्ह महँ कोई।
en: Kee tumh hari daasanh mahan koee |
mean: 'Are you one of Hari's devotees? My heart feels great love for you.'
'Or are you Ram himself, lover of the humble, come to bless me?'

label: दोहा 6
hi: तब हनुमंत कही सब राम कथा निज नाम।
सुनत जुगल तन पुलक मन मगन सुमिरि गुन ग्राम॥
en: Tab hanumant kahee sab raam kathaa nij naam |
Sunat jugal tan pulak man magan sumiri gun graam ||
mean: Then Hanuman told him all about Ram and gave his own name; both thrilled with joy, their minds immersed in Ram's virtues.
'Listen, son of the Wind, to how I live here - like a poor tongue among the teeth.'
'Friend, will the Lord of the Sun dynasty ever take pity on me as one without protection?'

hi: प्रीति न पद सरोज मन माहीं॥
en: Preeti na pad saroj man maaheen ||
mean: 'My body is of a dark nature; I have no spiritual practice and no love for his lotus feet.'
'But now I have hope, Hanuman, for one does not meet saints without Hari's grace.'

hi: तौ तुम्ह मोहि दरसु हठि दीन्हा॥
en: Tau tumh mohi darasu hathi deenhaa ||
mean: 'Since Ram has been gracious, you have come to me of your own accord.'
Hanuman said, 'Listen, Vibhishan, to the Lord's way: he always loves his servants.'
'Tell me, am I of noble birth? A restless monkey, lacking in every way.'

hi: तेहि दिन ताहि न मिलै अहारा॥
en: Tehi din taahi na milai ahaaraa ||
mean: 'Whoever says my name in the morning goes without food that day.'

label: दोहा 7
hi: अस मैं अधम सखा सुनु मोहू पर रघुबीर।
कीन्ही कृपा सुमिरि गुन भरे बिलोचन नीर॥
en: As main adham sakhaa sunu mohoo par raghubeer |
Keenhee kripaa sumiri gun bhare bilochan neer ||
mean: 'Friend, even on a lowly one like me Ram has shown grace.' Remembering his virtues, Hanuman's eyes filled with tears.

hi: फिरहिं ते काहे न होहिं दुखारी॥
en: Phirahin te kaahe na hohin dukhaaree ||
mean: 'Those who know such a master yet forget him and wander - how can they not suffer?'

hi: एहि बिधि कहत राम गुन ग्रामा।
en: Ehi bidhi kahat raam gun graamaa |
mean: Speaking thus of Ram's virtues, they found a peace beyond words.
Then Vibhishan told the whole story of how Sita was living there.
Hanuman said, 'Listen, brother, I wish to see Mother Janaki.'
Vibhishan explained how to do it, and Hanuman took leave and set off.

hi: करि सोइ रूप गयउ पुनि तहवाँ।
en: Kari soi roop gayau puni tahavaan |
mean: Taking that same tiny form, he went to the Ashok grove where Sita stayed.
Seeing her, he bowed in his heart; she sat as the watches of the night passed.

hi: कृस तन सीस जटा एक बेनी।
en: Kris tan sees jataa ek benee |
mean: Her body was frail, her hair a single matted braid, and in her heart she recited Ram's virtues.

label: दोहा 8
hi: निज पद नयन दिएँ मन राम पद कमल लीन।
परम दुखी भा पवनसुत देखि जानकी दीन॥
en: Nij pad nayan dien man raam pad kamal leen |
Param dukhee bhaa pavanasut dekhi jaanakee deen ||
mean: Eyes fixed on her own feet, mind absorbed in Ram's lotus feet - seeing Janaki so forlorn, Hanuman was deeply grieved.
He hid among the leaves of a tree, thinking, 'What should I do?'
Just then Ravan arrived, adorned, with many women.
The wicked one tried in many ways to persuade Sita - with coaxing, gifts, threats and division.
Ravan said, 'Listen, wise and lovely one: Mandodari and all my queens...'
'...I vow to make your servants. Just look at me once.'
Placing a blade of grass between them, and remembering her beloved Lord of Ayodhya, Sita said:
'Listen, ten-headed one: can a firefly's glow ever make the lotus bloom?'

hi: खल सुधि नहिं रघुबीर बान की॥
en: Khal sudhi nahin raghubeer baan kee ||
mean: 'Think on this,' said Janaki. 'Wretch, you have no idea of Ram's arrows.'
'Fool, you carried me off when no one was near. Shameless villain, have you no shame?'

label: दोहा 9
hi: आपुहि सुनि खद्योत सम रामहि भानु समान।
परुष बचन सुनि काढ़ि असि बोला अति खिसिआन॥
en: Aapuhi suni khadyot sam raamahi bhaanu samaan |
Parush bachan suni kaadhi asi bolaa ati khisiaan ||
mean: Hearing himself called a firefly and Ram the sun, and stung by her harsh words, Ravan drew his sword in fury.
'Sita, you have insulted me. I will cut off your head with this cruel sword.'

hi: नाहिं त सपदि मानु मम बानी।
सुमुखि होति न त जीवन हानी॥
en: Naahin ta sapadi maanu mam baanee |
Sumukhi hoti na ta jeevan haanee ||
mean: 'Otherwise, accept my words at once, lovely one, or you will lose your life.'

hi: प्रभु भुज करि कर सम दसकंधर॥
en: Prabhu bhuj kari kar sam dasakandhar ||
mean: Sita said: 'My Lord's arm, beautiful like a garland of dark lotuses and like an elephant's trunk, O ten-headed one...'

hi: सो भुज कंठ कि तव असि घोरा।
सुनु सठ अस प्रवान पन मोरा॥
en: So bhuj kanth ki tav asi ghoraa |
Sunu sath as pravaan pan moraa ||
mean: '...either that arm will be around my neck or your terrible sword. Hear my firm vow, fool.'
'O Chandrahas sword, take away my anguish, born of the fire of separation from Ram.'

hi: कह सीता हरु मम दुख भारा॥
en: Kah seetaa haru mam dukh bhaaraa ||
mean: 'You carry a cool, sharp edge - take away my heavy sorrow,' said Sita.
Hearing this he rushed to kill her, but Mandodari calmed him with wise counsel.
He called all the demonesses and told them, 'Go and frighten Sita in every way.'

hi: मास दिवस महुँ कहा न माना।
en: Maas divas mahun kahaa na maanaa |
mean: 'If she does not obey within a month, I will kill her with my sword.'

label: दोहा 10
hi: भवन गयउ दसकंधर इहाँ पिसाचिनि बृंद।
सीतहि त्रास देखावहि धरहिं रूप बहु मंद॥
en: Bhavan gayau dasakandhar ihaan pisaachini brind |
Seetahi traas dekhaavahi dharahin roop bahu mand ||
mean: Ravan went home; here the demonesses took many ugly forms to terrify Sita.
There was a demoness named Trijata, devoted to Ram's feet and wise in discernment.
She called them all and told them her dream: 'Serve Sita and save yourselves.'
'In my dream a monkey burned Lanka and killed the whole demon army.'
'Ravan rode a donkey, naked, his heads shaven and his twenty arms cut off.'

hi: एहि बिधि सो दच्छिन दिसि जाई।
en: Ehi bidhi so dachchhin disi jaaee |
mean: 'He went thus toward the south, and Lanka seemed to pass to Vibhishan.'
'Ram's victory was proclaimed through the city, and the Lord sent for Sita.'
'I tell you openly: this dream will come true in a few days.'

hi: तासु बचन सुनि ते सब डरीं।
en: Taasu bachan suni te sab dareen |
mean: Hearing her, they all grew afraid and fell at Janaki's feet.

label: दोहा 11
hi: जहँ तहँ गईं सकल तब सीता कर मन सोच।
मास दिवस बीतें मोहि मारिहि निसिचर पोच॥
en: Jahan tahan gaeen sakal tab seetaa kar man soch |
Maas divas beeten mohi maarihi nisichar poch ||
mean: They scattered, and Sita worried: 'When the month passes, the vile demon will kill me.'
Joining her palms she said to Trijata, 'Mother, you are my companion in trouble.'

hi: दुसहु बिरहु अब नहिं सहि जाई॥
en: Dusahu birahu ab nahin sahi jaaee ||
mean: 'Quickly find a way for me to leave this body; I cannot bear this separation any longer.'
'Bring wood and build a pyre, mother, then set it alight.'

hi: सुनै को श्रवन सूल सम बानी॥
en: Sunai ko shravan sool sam baanee ||
mean: 'Wise one, prove my love true. Who can bear to hear words that pierce like spears?'
Hearing this, Trijata held her feet and consoled her, telling her of the Lord's might and glory.

hi: निसि न अनल मिल सुनु सुकुमारी।
अस कहि सो निज भवन सिधारी॥
en: Nisi na anal mil sunu sukumaaree |
As kahi so nij bhavan sidhaaree ||
mean: 'Listen, gentle one, no fire can be had at night.' Saying this, she went home.

hi: मिलहि न पावक मिटिहि न सूला॥
en: Milahi na paavak mitihi na soolaa ||
mean: Sita said, 'Fate has turned against me; I can get no fire, and my pain will not end.'
'Embers are plainly visible in the sky, yet not one star comes down to earth.'
'Even the moon, made of fire, rains none on me - as if it knows I am unfortunate.'

hi: सत्य नाम करु हरु मम सोका॥
en: Saty naam karu haru mam sokaa ||
mean: 'Hear my plea, Ashok tree: make your name true (sorrowless) and take away my sorrow.'
'Your new leaves are like flames; give me fire and do not be cruel.'

hi: सो छन कपिहि कलप सम बीता॥
en: So chhan kapihi kalap sam beetaa ||
mean: Seeing Sita so stricken by separation, each moment passed like an age for Hanuman.

label: दोहा 12
hi: कपि करि हृदयँ बिचार दीन्हि मुद्रिका डारी तब।
जनु असोक अंगार दीन्हि हरषि उठि कर गहेउ॥
en: Kapi kari hridayan bichaar deenhi mudrikaa daaree tab |
Janu asok angaar deenhi harashi uthi kar gaheu ||
mean: Thinking it over, Hanuman dropped the ring; Sita, as if the Ashok tree had given her an ember, rose joyfully and took it in her hand.
Then she saw the lovely ring, beautifully engraved with Ram's name.
Astonished, she recognised the ring; joy and grief together troubled her heart.

hi: माया तें असि रचि नहिं जाई॥
en: Maayaa ten asi rachi nahin jaaee ||
mean: 'Who could defeat the invincible Ram? Yet no illusion could create such a ring.'
As Sita weighed many thoughts, Hanuman spoke in sweet words.
He began describing Ram's virtues; hearing them, Sita's sorrow fled.
She listened with all her heart as he told the whole story from the beginning.

hi: कहि सो प्रगट होति किन भाई॥
en: Kahi so pragat hoti kin bhaaee ||
mean: 'You who told this story, nectar to my ears - why don't you show yourself, brother?'
Then Hanuman came near; she turned away, astonished.
'I am Ram's messenger, Mother Janaki; I swear by the Lord of compassion.'
'Mother, I brought this ring; Ram gave it to me as a token for you.'
'Tell me how man and monkey came together.' He told her how their friendship began.

label: दोहा 13
hi: कपि के बचन सप्रेम सुनि उपजा मन बिस्वास।
जाना मन क्रम बचन यह कृपासिंधु कर दास॥
en: Kapi ke bachan saprem suni upajaa man bisvaas |
Jaanaa man kram bachan yah kripaasindhu kar daas ||
mean: Hearing the monkey's loving words, faith arose in her: she knew in thought, word and deed that he was a servant of the ocean of mercy.
Knowing him to be the Lord's devotee, her love grew deep; her eyes filled and her body thrilled.
'Hanuman, as I was drowning in the ocean of separation, you have become my boat.'
'Now tell me - bless you - are Ram and his brother well and happy?'
'Ram is tender-hearted and kind; why has he become so hard, Hanuman?'
'It is his nature to bring joy to his servants. Does he ever remember me?'
'Will my eyes ever be soothed by seeing his dark, gentle form?'

hi: बचनु न आव नयन भरे बारी।
en: Bachanu na aav nayan bhare baaree |
mean: Words failed her and her eyes filled: 'Alas, my Lord has utterly forgotten me.'
Seeing Sita so overcome, Hanuman spoke gently and humbly:
'Mother, the Lord and his brother are well; that home of mercy grieves at your grief.'

hi: तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना॥
en: Tumh te premu raam ken doonaa ||
mean: 'Mother, do not think his love is less - Ram loves you twice as much as you love him.'

label: दोहा 14
hi: रघुपति कर संदेसु अब सुनु जननी धरि धीर।
अस कहि कपि गद गद भयउ भरे बिलोचन नीर॥
en: Raghupati kar sandesu ab sunu jananee dhari dheer |
As kahi kapi gad gad bhayau bhare bilochan neer ||
mean: 'Mother, now hear Ram's message and take heart.' Saying this, Hanuman was choked with emotion and his eyes filled with tears.
Ram said: 'Sita, in your absence everything has turned against me.'
'Fresh leaves seem like fire, the night like the night of doom, the moon like the scorching sun.'
'Lotus groves seem like forests of spears, and clouds seem to rain boiling oil.'

hi: जे हित रहे करत तेइ पीरा।
en: Je hit rahe karat tei peeraa |
mean: 'What once comforted me now gives pain; the gentle breeze feels like a serpent's breath.'

hi: कहेहू तें कछु दुख घटि होई।
काहि कहौं यह जान न कोई॥
en: Kahehoo ten kachhu dukh ghati hoee |
Kaahi kahaun yah jaan na koee ||
mean: 'Speaking of it might ease the pain a little, but whom can I tell? No one understands.'

hi: तत्व प्रेम कर मम अरु तोरा।
en: Tatv prem kar mam aru toraa |
mean: 'The truth of the love between you and me, my beloved, only my mind knows.'

hi: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं।
en: So manu sadaa rahat tohi paaheen |
mean: 'And that mind always stays with you - know the essence of my love in this alone.'

hi: मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही॥
en: Magan prem tan sudhi nahin tehee ||
mean: Hearing the Lord's message, Sita was so lost in love she forgot her body.

hi: कह कपि हृदयँ धीर धरु माता।
en: Kah kapi hridayan dheer dharu maataa |
mean: Hanuman said, 'Mother, take heart; remember Ram, who brings joy to his servants.'
'Hold the Lord's might in your heart, hear my words and give up fear.'

label: दोहा 15
hi: निसिचर निकर पतंग सम रघुपति बान कृसानु।
जननी हृदयँ धीर धरु जरे निसाचर जानु॥
en: Nisichar nikar patang sam raghupati baan krisaanu |
Jananee hridayan dheer dharu jare nisaachar jaanu ||
mean: 'Mother, the demon hordes are like moths and Ram's arrows like fire. Take heart - know the demons as already burnt.'
'Had Ram received news of you, he would not have delayed.'
'When the sun of Ram's arrows rises, Janaki, where will the darkness of demons be?'
'I could take you away right now, mother, but I swear by Ram I have no such order.'
'Be patient a few days, mother; Ram will come with the monkey army.'
'He will kill the demons and take you back; Narad and others will sing his glory in the three worlds.'

hi: हैं सुत कपि सब तुम्हहि समाना।
en: Hain sut kapi sab tumhahi samaanaa |
mean: Sita said, 'Son, all the monkeys must be like you, and the demons are mighty warriors.'

hi: सुनि कपि प्रगट कीन्ह निज देहा॥
en: Suni kapi pragat keenh nij dehaa ||
mean: 'My heart has great doubt.' Hearing this, Hanuman revealed his true form.
His body was like a golden mountain - a mighty hero, terrible in battle.
Then Sita's heart was reassured, and the Wind's son took his small form again.

label: दोहा 16
hi: सुनु माता साखामृग नहिं बल बुद्धि बिसाल।
प्रभु प्रताप तें गरुड़हि खाइ परम लघु ब्याल॥
en: Sunu maataa saakhaamrig nahin bal buddhi bisaal |
Prabhu prataap ten garudahi khaai param laghu byaal ||
mean: 'Listen, mother: monkeys have no great strength or wisdom. By the Lord's glory, even a tiny snake can devour Garud.'
Sita was content hearing his words, filled with devotion, glory, radiance and strength.
Knowing him dear to Ram, she blessed him: 'Son, be a treasure of strength and virtue.'
'Be ageless, immortal and full of virtues, son, and may Ram shower his love on you.'

hi: करहुँ कृपा प्रभु अस सुनि काना।
en: Karahun kripaa prabhu as suni kaanaa |
mean: Hearing 'May the Lord be gracious to you,' Hanuman was lost in complete love.
Again and again he bowed his head at her feet and, with joined palms, said:
'Mother, now my life is fulfilled; your blessing is known to be unfailing.'
'Mother, I am very hungry, seeing the lovely fruits on these trees.'
'Son, very mighty demon warriors guard this garden.'

hi: तिन्ह कर भय माता मोहि नाहीं।
जौं तुम्ह सुख मानहु मन माहीं॥
en: Tinh kar bhay maataa mohi naaheen |
Jaun tumh sukh maanahu man maaheen ||
mean: 'Mother, I have no fear of them, if only you are pleased in your heart.'

label: दोहा 17
hi: देखि बुद्धि बल निपुन कपि कहेउ जानकीं जाहु।
रघुपति चरन हृदयँ धरि तात मधुर फल खाहु॥
en: Dekhi buddhi bal nipun kapi kaheu jaanakeen jaahu |
Raghupati charan hridayan dhari taat madhur phal khaahu ||
mean: Seeing his wisdom and strength, Janaki said, 'Go, son, and eat the sweet fruits, keeping Ram's feet in your heart.'
Bowing, he went into the garden, ate the fruit and began breaking the trees.
Many guards were there; some he killed, and some ran to raise the alarm.
'Lord, a huge monkey has come and wrecked the Ashok grove.'
'He ate the fruit, uprooted the trees, and crushed the guards to the ground.'
Hearing this, Ravan sent many warriors; seeing them, Hanuman roared.
Hanuman destroyed all the demons; a few, half-dead, ran away crying out.
Then Ravan sent prince Akshay, who set out with countless warriors.
Seeing him come, Hanuman seized a tree, challenged him, struck him down and roared mightily.

label: दोहा 18
hi: कछु मारेसि कछु मर्देसि कछु मिलएसि धरि धूरि।
कछु पुनि जाइ पुकारे प्रभु मर्कट बल भूरि॥
en: Kachhu maaresi kachhu mardesi kachhu milaesi dhari dhoori |
Kachhu puni jaai pukaare prabhu markat bal bhoori ||
mean: Some he killed, some he crushed, some he ground into the dust; others went and cried, 'Lord, the monkey's strength is immense!'
Hearing of his son's death, Ravan was enraged and sent the mighty Meghnad.
'Do not kill him, son - bind him. Let us see where this monkey comes from.'
Indrajit, the matchless warrior, set out, angry at his brother's death.
Hanuman saw the fierce warrior coming, gnashed his teeth, roared and charged.
He uprooted a huge tree and left Ravan's son without his chariot.

hi: गहि गहि कपि मर्दइ निज अंगा॥
en: Gahi gahi kapi mardai nij angaa ||
mean: Great warriors were with him; Hanuman seized them one by one and crushed them against his body.
Having felled them, he fought Meghnad - the two clashed like great elephants.
Striking him with his fist, Hanuman climbed a tree; Meghnad fainted for a moment.
Rising again, Meghnad used many illusions, but the son of the Wind could not be defeated.

label: दोहा 19
hi: ब्रह्म अस्त्र तेहिं साँधा कपि मन कीन्ह बिचार।
जौं न ब्रह्मसर मानउँ महिमा मिटइ अपार॥
en: Brahm astr tehin saandhaa kapi man keenh bichaar |
Jaun na brahmasar maanaun mahimaa mitai apaar ||
mean: Meghnad aimed the Brahmastra; Hanuman thought, 'If I do not honour Brahma's weapon, its great glory will be lost.'
Meghnad struck Hanuman with the Brahma weapon; even as he fell, Hanuman crushed many soldiers.
Seeing Hanuman faint, Meghnad bound him with the serpent noose and took him away.
(Shiva says:) Listen, Bhavani: by chanting his name, the wise cut the bonds of worldly life.

hi: तासु दूत कि बंध तरु आवा।
en: Taasu doot ki bandh taru aavaa |
mean: Could his messenger ever be bound? Hanuman let himself be tied for the Lord's work.
Hearing the monkey was bound, the demons rushed to Ravan's court to watch the spectacle.

hi: कहि न जाइ कछु अति प्रभुताई॥
en: Kahi na jaai kachhu ati prabhutaaee ||
mean: Hanuman saw Ravan's court; its splendour was beyond words.
Gods and guardians of the directions stood humbly with joined palms, all anxiously watching Ravan's brow.

hi: देखि प्रताप न कपि मन संका।
en: Dekhi prataap na kapi man sankaa |
mean: Seeing his might, Hanuman felt no fear, like Garud fearless among serpents.

label: दोहा 20
hi: कपिहि बिलोकि दसानन बिहसा कहि दुर्बाद।
सुत बध सुरति कीन्हि पुनि उपजा हृदयँ बिषाद॥
en: Kapihi biloki dasaanan bihasaa kahi durbaad |
Sut badh surati keenhi puni upajaa hridayan bishaad ||
mean: Seeing the monkey, Ravan laughed and spoke insults; then, remembering his son's death, grief rose in his heart.

hi: केहिं के बल घालेहि बन खीसा॥
en: Kehin ke bal ghaalehi ban kheesaa ||
mean: Ravan said, 'Who are you, monkey? On whose strength did you destroy my garden?'

hi: की धौं श्रवन सुनेहि नहिं मोही।
en: Kee dhaun shravan sunehi nahin mohee |
mean: 'Have you never heard of me? I see you are utterly fearless, fool.'

hi: कहु सठ तोहि न प्रान कइ बाधा॥
en: Kahu sath tohi na praan kai baadhaa ||
mean: 'For what offence did you kill the demons? Tell me, fool, do you not fear for your life?'
Hanuman said: 'Listen, Ravan - he by whose power Maya creates countless universes...'
'...by whose power Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva create, sustain and destroy, O ten-headed one...'
'...by whose power the thousand-headed Shesh carries the universe with its mountains and forests on his head...'
'...who takes many forms to protect the gods and to teach fools like you...'

hi: तेहि समेत नृप दल मद गंजा॥
en: Tehi samet nrip dal mad ganjaa ||
mean: '...who broke Shiva's mighty bow and crushed the pride of the assembled kings...'
'...who killed Khar, Dushan, Trishira and Bali, all of matchless strength...'

label: दोहा 21
hi: जाके बल लवलेस तें जितेहु चराचर झारि।
तासु दूत मैं जा करि हरि आनेहु प्रिय नारि॥
en: Jaake bal lavales ten jitehu charaachar jhaari |
Taasu doot main jaa kari hari aanehu priy naari ||
mean: '...by a fraction of whose strength you conquered the whole world - I am his messenger, whose beloved wife you have stolen.'
'I know your greatness: how you fought Sahasrabahu...'

hi: समर बालि सन करि जसु पावा।
en: Samar baali san kari jasu paavaa |
mean: '...and how you won fame fighting Bali.' Ravan laughed off the monkey's words.
'I ate the fruit because I was hungry, lord, and broke the trees as monkeys do.'

hi: सब कें देह परम प्रिय स्वामी।
en: Sab ken deh param priy svaamee |
mean: 'Everyone holds his body very dear, master; those wicked ones attacked me...'

hi: जिन्ह मोहि मारा ते मैं मारे।
en: Jinh mohi maaraa te main maare |
mean: '...so I struck those who struck me. And then your son bound me.'

hi: मोहि न कछु बाँधे कइ लाजा।
कीन्ह चहउँ निज प्रभु कर काजा॥
en: Mohi na kachhu baandhe kai laajaa |
Keenh chahaun nij prabhu kar kaajaa ||
mean: 'I feel no shame at being bound; I only wish to do my Lord's work.'
'Ravan, I beg you with joined palms: give up your pride and hear my advice.'

hi: भ्रम तजि भजहु भगत भय हारी॥
en: Bhram taji bhajahu bhagat bhay haaree ||
mean: 'Think of your own lineage; give up delusion and worship him who removes his devotees' fear.'
'He whom even Death fears greatly - Death who devours gods, demons and all creatures...'
'...never make an enemy of him. Listen to me and give Janaki back.'

label: दोहा 22
hi: गएँ सरन प्रभु राखिहैं तव अपराध बिसारि॥
en: Gaen saran prabhu raakhihain tav aparaadh bisaari ||
mean: 'Ram, protector of those who bow to him, ocean of mercy, slayer of Khar - if you seek refuge, he will forget your offences and protect you.'
'Hold Ram's lotus feet in your heart and rule Lanka forever.'

hi: तेहि ससि महुँ जनि होहु कलंका॥
en: Tehi sasi mahun jani hohu kalankaa ||
mean: 'Sage Pulastya's fame is like a spotless moon; do not become a stain on that moon.'

hi: राम नाम बिनु गिरा न सोहा।
en: Raam naam binu giraa na sohaa |
mean: 'Without Ram's name, speech has no beauty. Think it over, giving up pride and delusion.'
'O enemy of the gods, even a lovely woman adorned with every jewel looks poor without clothing.'
'Wealth and power of one who turns from Ram go as if never gained.'
'Rivers with no spring at their source dry up as soon as the rains are over.'
'Listen, Ravan, I declare this on oath: no one can save one who has turned against Ram.'

hi: सकहिं न राखि राम कर द्रोही॥
en: Sakahin na raakhi raam kar drohee ||
mean: 'Even a thousand Shivas, Vishnus and Brahmas cannot protect an enemy of Ram.'

label: दोहा 23
hi: मोहमूल बहु सूल प्रद त्यागहु तम अभिमान।
भजहु राम रघुनायक कृपा सिंधु भगवान॥
en: Mohamool bahu sool prad tyaagahu tam abhimaan |
Bhajahu raam raghunaayak kripaa sindhu bhagavaan ||
mean: 'Give up dark pride, root of delusion and source of much pain, and worship Ram, Lord of Raghus, ocean of mercy.'

hi: जदपि कहि कपि अति हित बानी।
en: Jadapi kahi kapi ati hit baanee |
mean: Though Hanuman spoke very beneficial words, full of devotion, wisdom, detachment and good sense...

hi: मिला हमहि कपि गुर बड़ ग्यानी॥
en: Milaa hamahi kapi gur bad gyaanee ||
mean: ...the arrogant Ravan laughed: 'We have found a very learned monkey for a guru!'
'Wretch, your death is near, that you, lowly one, presume to teach me.'
Hanuman said, 'It will be the reverse; I clearly see your mind is deluded.'

hi: बेगि न हरहुँ मूढ़ कर प्राना॥
en: Begi na harahun moodh kar praanaa ||
mean: Stung by his words, Ravan said, 'Why doesn't someone quickly kill this fool?'
Hearing this, demons ran to kill him; just then Vibhishan arrived with ministers.
Bowing his head and pleading humbly, he said, 'It is against good conduct to kill a messenger.'
'Give him some other punishment, master.' Everyone agreed this was good advice.
Hearing this, Ravan laughed: 'Then send the monkey back maimed.'

label: दोहा 24
hi: कपि कें ममता पूँछ पर सबहि कहउँ समुझाइ।
तेल बोरि पट बाँधि पुनि पावक देहु लगाइ॥
en: Kapi ken mamataa poonchh par sabahi kahaun samujhaai |
Tel bori pat baandhi puni paavak dehu lagaai ||
mean: 'A monkey loves his tail, I tell you all - wrap it in oil-soaked cloth and set it on fire.'

hi: तब सठ निज नाथहि लइ आइहि॥
en: Tab sath nij naathahi lai aaihi ||
mean: 'When the tailless monkey goes back there, the fool will bring his master here.'
'I shall see the might of the one he praised so much.'
Hearing this, Hanuman smiled inwardly: 'I see Saraswati has come to help me.'
Hearing Ravan's words, the foolish demons began to carry out the plan.

hi: रहा न नगर बसन घृत तेला।
en: Rahaa na nagar basan ghrit telaa |
mean: No cloth, ghee or oil was left in the city, for the monkey playfully made his tail grow.
The townspeople came to watch, kicking him and laughing loudly.
Drums beat and all clapped; they paraded him through the city and set his tail alight.
Seeing the fire blazing, Hanuman at once became very small.
Slipping free, he leapt onto the golden mansions; the demon women grew afraid.

label: दोहा 25
hi: हरि प्रेरित तेहि अवसर चले मरुत उनचास।
अट्टहास करि गर्ज़ा कपि बढ़ि लाग अकास॥
en: Hari prerit tehi avasar chale marut unachaas |
Attahaas kari garzaa kapi badhi laag akaas ||
mean: At that moment, sent by Hari, all forty-nine winds began to blow; Hanuman laughed aloud, roared, and grew until he touched the sky.
Huge yet very light, he raced from palace to palace.
The city burned and people were in despair; countless fierce flames leapt up.
Cries rang out: 'Oh father! Oh mother! Who will save us now?'

hi: हम जो कहा यह कपि नहिं होई।
en: Ham jo kahaa yah kapi nahin hoee |
mean: 'Didn't we say this is no monkey but some god in a monkey's form?'
'Such is the fruit of insulting a saint - the city burns as if it had no protector.'
He burned the city in an instant; only Vibhishan's house was spared.

hi: ता कर दूत अनल जेहिं सिरिजा।
जरा न सो तेहि कारन गिरिजा॥
en: Taa kar doot anal jehin sirijaa |
Jaraa na so tehi kaaran girijaa ||
mean: (Shiva says:) Girija, Hanuman was not burned because he is the messenger of the one who created fire.
Turning this way and that, he burned all Lanka, then leapt into the sea.

label: दोहा 26
hi: पूँछ बुझाइ खोइ श्रम धरि लघु रूप बहोरि।
जनकसुता के आगें ठाढ़ भयउ कर जोरि॥
en: Poonchh bujhaai khoi shram dhari laghu roop bahori |
Janakasutaa ke aagen thaadh bhayau kar jori ||
mean: Putting out his tail and shaking off weariness, he took a small form again and stood before Janaki with joined palms.
'Mother, give me some token, as Ram gave me one.'
Then she took off her crest-jewel and gave it; Hanuman received it joyfully.
'Son, give my salutations to the Lord thus: Lord, you lack nothing in every way...'
'...yet, remembering your vow to be kind to the humble, Lord, remove my great distress.'
'Son, tell him the story of Indra's son and remind the Lord of the power of his arrow.'

hi: मास दिवस महुँ नाथु न आवा।
तौ पुनि मोहि जिअत नहिं पावा॥
en: Maas divas mahun naathu na aavaa |
Tau puni mohi jiat nahin paavaa ||
mean: 'If my Lord does not come within a month, he will not find me alive.'

hi: कहु कपि केहि बिधि राखौं प्राना।
en: Kahu kapi kehi bidhi raakhaun praanaa |
mean: 'Tell me, Hanuman, how can I hold on to life? Now you too speak of leaving.'

hi: पुनि मो कहुँ सोइ दिनु सो राती॥
en: Puni mo kahun soi dinu so raatee ||
mean: 'Seeing you, my heart was soothed; now the same days and nights will return for me.'

label: दोहा 27
hi: जनकसुतहि समुझाइ करि बहु बिधि धीरजु दीन्ह।
चरन कमल सिरु नाइ कपि गवनु राम पहिं कीन्ह॥
en: Janakasutahi samujhaai kari bahu bidhi dheeraju deenh |
Charan kamal siru naai kapi gavanu raam pahin keenh ||
mean: Hanuman consoled Janaki and gave her courage in many ways; then, bowing at her lotus feet, he set out for Ram.
As he left he roared mightily; hearing it, the demon women miscarried in fear.
Crossing the ocean he reached this shore and let out a joyful cry for the monkeys to hear.
Seeing Hanuman, all rejoiced; the monkeys felt they had been born anew.
His face was cheerful and his body shone: he had done Ram's work.
They all met him with great joy, like a gasping fish finding water.
Joyfully they set off for Ram, asking and hearing the new tale.
Then they all entered Madhuban and, with Angad's consent, ate honey and fruits.
When the guards tried to stop them, they struck them with fists and the guards fled.

label: दोहा 28
hi: जाइ पुकारे ते सब बन उजार जुबराज।
सुनि सुग्रीव हरष कपि करि आए प्रभु काज॥
en: Jaai pukaare te sab ban ujaar jubaraaj |
Suni sugreev harash kapi kari aae prabhu kaaj ||
mean: The guards went and complained, 'The prince is wrecking the garden.' Sugriv rejoiced, knowing the monkeys had done the Lord's work.

hi: जौं न होति सीता सुधि पाई।
मधुबन के फल सकहिं कि खाई॥
en: Jaun na hoti seetaa sudhi paaee |
Madhuban ke phal sakahin ki khaaee ||
mean: 'If they had not found news of Sita, would they dare eat the fruits of Madhuban?'

hi: एहि बिधि मन बिचार कर राजा।
en: Ehi bidhi man bichaar kar raajaa |
mean: While the king thought this, the monkeys arrived with their whole party.
They all came and bowed at his feet; Sugriv met them all with great love.
He asked after them; they said, 'Seeing your feet, all is well. By Ram's grace the task is done.'
'Lord, Hanuman did the work and saved the lives of all the monkeys.'
Hearing this, Sugriv embraced Hanuman again and went with the monkeys to Ram.
When Ram saw the monkeys coming, having done the task, his heart was very glad.
The two brothers sat on a crystal rock; all the monkeys went and fell at their feet.

label: दोहा 29
hi: प्रीति सहित सब भेटे रघुपति करुना पुंज।
पूँछी कुसल नाथ अब कुसल देखि पद कंज॥
en: Preeti sahit sab bhete raghupati karunaa punj |
Poonchhee kusal naath ab kusal dekhi pad kanj ||
mean: Ram, full of compassion, met them all lovingly and asked after them. They said, 'Lord, seeing your lotus feet, now all is well.'

hi: जा पर नाथ करहु तुम्ह दाया॥
en: Jaa par naath karahu tumh daayaa ||
mean: Jambavan said: 'Listen, Lord of Raghus - one on whom you show kindness...'

hi: सुर नर मुनि प्रसन्न ता ऊपर॥
en: Sur nar muni prasann taa oopar ||
mean: '...always enjoys good fortune and well-being; gods, men and sages are pleased with him.'
'He is victorious, humble and an ocean of virtues; his fame lights up the three worlds.'

hi: प्रभु कीं कृपा भयउ सबु काजू।
en: Prabhu keen kripaa bhayau sabu kaajoo |
mean: 'By the Lord's grace the whole task is done; today our lives are fulfilled.'

hi: सहसहुँ मुख न जाइ सो बरनी॥
en: Sahasahun mukh na jaai so baranee ||
mean: 'Lord, what Hanuman did cannot be described even with a thousand mouths.'
Jambavan then told Ram of the Wind's son's glorious deeds.
Hearing them, the merciful Lord was delighted and joyfully embraced Hanuman.
'Tell me, son, how does Janaki live? How does she keep herself alive?'

label: दोहा 30
hi: नाम पाहरु दिवस निसि ध्यान तुम्हार कपाट।
लोचन निज पद जंत्रित जाहिं प्रान केहिं बाट॥
en: Naam paaharu divas nisi dhyaan tumhaar kapaat |
Lochan nij pad jantrit jaahin praan kehin baat ||
mean: 'Your name guards her day and night, meditation on you is the door, her eyes are fixed on her feet - by what path could her life escape?'
'As I left she gave me her crest-jewel.' Ram took it and held it to his heart.
'Lord, with both eyes full of tears, Janaki said a few words:'
'Hold the Lord's feet, with his brother, and say: friend of the humble, remover of the distress of those who bow...'
'...I love your feet in thought, word and deed. For what fault, Lord, have you abandoned me?'
'I admit one fault of mine: my life did not leave when we were separated.'
'But Lord, that is my eyes' fault: they stubbornly stop my life from leaving.'
'The fire of separation, my body like cotton, my breath the wind - this body would burn in a moment...'

hi: नयन स्त्रवहि जलु निज हित लागी।
en: Nayan stravahi jalu nij hit laagee |
mean: '...but my eyes shed tears for their own sake, so my body cannot burn in that fire.'
'Sita's distress is immense; it is better left unsaid, O kind to the humble.'

label: दोहा 31
hi: निमिष निमिष करुनानिधि जाहिं कलप सम बीति।
बेगि चलिय प्रभु आनिअ भुज बल खल दल जीति॥
en: Nimish nimish karunaanidhi jaahin kalap sam beeti |
Begi chaliy prabhu aania bhuj bal khal dal jeeti ||
mean: 'O ocean of mercy, every moment passes for her like an age. Go quickly, Lord, defeat the wicked by the strength of your arms and bring her back.'

hi: सुनि सीता दुख प्रभु सुख अयना।
en: Suni seetaa dukh prabhu sukh ayanaa |
mean: Hearing of Sita's sorrow, the Lord, home of joy, had tears in his lotus eyes.

hi: बचन काँय मन मम गति जाही।
en: Bachan kaany man mam gati jaahee |
mean: 'Can one whose only refuge in word, body and mind is me ever know distress, even in a dream?'

hi: जब तव सुमिरन भजन न होई॥
en: Jab tav sumiran bhajan na hoee ||
mean: Hanuman said, 'Lord, the only real distress is when one fails to remember and worship you.'
'What are the demons to you, Lord? You will defeat the enemy and bring back Janaki.'

hi: नहिं कोउ सुर नर मुनि तनुधारी॥
en: Nahin kou sur nar muni tanudhaaree ||
mean: Ram said, 'Listen, Hanuman: no god, man or sage in bodily form has done me such a service.'

hi: सनमुख होइ न सकत मन मोरा॥
en: Sanamukh hoi na sakat man moraa ||
mean: 'How can I repay you? My heart cannot even face you.'
'Listen, son, I have thought it over in my heart: I can never be free of this debt.'
The protector of the gods gazed at Hanuman again and again, eyes wet and body thrilling.

label: दोहा 32
hi: सुनि प्रभु बचन बिलोकि मुख गात हरषि हनुमंत।
चरन परेउ प्रेमाकुल त्राहि त्राहि भगवंत॥
en: Suni prabhu bachan biloki mukh gaat harashi hanumant |
Charan pareu premaakul traahi traahi bhagavant ||
mean: Hearing the Lord's words and seeing his face and form, Hanuman, overwhelmed with love, fell at his feet crying, 'Save me, save me, Lord!'

hi: प्रेम मगन तेहि उठब न भावा॥
en: Prem magan tehi uthab na bhaavaa ||
mean: Again and again the Lord tried to raise him, but lost in love he did not wish to rise.

hi: प्रभु कर पंकज कपि कें सीसा।
en: Prabhu kar pankaj kapi ken seesaa |
mean: The Lord's lotus hand on Hanuman's head - remembering that scene, Shiva was lost in rapture.
Collecting himself, Shiva continued the beautiful story.
Raising Hanuman, the Lord embraced him and, holding his hand, seated him very close.

hi: केहि बिधि दहेउ दुर्ग अति बंका॥
en: Kehi bidhi daheu durg ati bankaa ||
mean: 'Tell me, Hanuman, how did you burn Ravan's Lanka, that most impregnable fortress?'
Seeing the Lord pleased, Hanuman spoke without any pride:
'The greatest skill of a monkey is just to leap from branch to branch.'
'Crossing the ocean, burning the golden city, killing demons and wrecking the grove...'
'...all of it was your glory, Lord of Raghus. None of it was my own might.'

label: दोहा 33
hi: ता कहुँ प्रभु कछु अगम नहिं जा पर तुम्ह अनुकुल।
तब प्रभावँ बड़वानलहिं जारि सकइ खलु तूल॥
en: Taa kahun prabhu kachhu agam nahin jaa par tumh anukul |
Tab prabhaavan badavaanalahin jaari sakai khalu tool ||
mean: 'Lord, nothing is out of reach for one you favour; by your power even cotton can burn up the ocean fire.'
'Lord, graciously grant me unwavering devotion, which gives the highest joy.'

hi: सुनि प्रभु परम सरल कपि बानी।
en: Suni prabhu param saral kapi baanee |
mean: (Shiva says:) Bhavani, hearing Hanuman's simple words, the Lord said, 'So be it.'

hi: ताहि भजनु तजि भाव न आना॥
en: Taahi bhajanu taji bhaav na aanaa ||
mean: Uma, one who knows Ram's nature cares for nothing but worshipping him.
Whoever takes this dialogue to heart gains devotion to Ram's feet.
Hearing the Lord's words, the monkeys cried, 'Victory, victory, victory to the merciful source of joy!'
Then Ram called Sugriv and said, 'Prepare for the march.'
'Why delay any longer? Give the order to the monkeys at once.'

hi: नभ तें भवन चले सुर हरषी॥
en: Nabh ten bhavan chale sur harashee ||
mean: Watching this, the gods showered flowers and returned joyfully from the sky to their homes.

label: दोहा 34
hi: कपिपति बेगि बोलाए आए जूथप जूथ।
नाना बरन अतुल बल बानर भालु बरूथ॥
en: Kapipati begi bolaae aae joothap jooth |
Naanaa baran atul bal baanar bhaalu barooth ||
mean: Sugriv quickly summoned them, and the commanders came with their troops - hosts of monkeys and bears of many colours and matchless strength.
They bowed at the Lord's lotus feet; the mighty bears and monkeys roared.
Ram looked over the whole monkey army, gazing on it with his gracious lotus eyes.
Strengthened by Ram's grace, the monkey chiefs seemed like mountains with wings.
Then Ram joyfully set out, and many fine auspicious omens appeared.
For one whose glory is all auspicious, good omens on his march are only natural.

hi: फरकि बाम अँग जनु कहि देहीं॥
en: Pharaki baam ang janu kahi deheen ||
mean: Sita sensed the Lord's departure - her left side throbbed as if telling her.
Every good omen that came to Janaki was a bad omen for Ravan.
The army moved - who can describe it? Countless monkeys and bears roared.
Armed with claws, carrying rocks and trees, they moved at will through sky and land.
The bears and monkeys roared like lions; the elephants of the directions reeled and trumpeted.

label: छंद 1
hi: चिक्करहिं दिग्गज डोल महि गिरि लोल सागर खरभरे।
मन हरष सभ गंधर्ब सुर मुनि नाग किन्नर दुख टरे॥
कटकटहिं मर्कट बिकट भट बहु कोटि कोटिन्ह धावहीं।
जय राम प्रबल प्रताप कोसलनाथ गुन गन गावहीं॥1॥
en: Chikkarahin diggaj dol mahi giri lol saagar kharabhare |
Man harash sabh gandharb sur muni naag kinnar dukh tare ||
Katakatahin markat bikat bhat bahu koti kotinh dhaavaheen |
Jay raam prabal prataap kosalanaath gun gan gaavaheen || 1 ||
mean: The elephants of the quarters trumpeted, the earth shook, mountains swayed and the seas churned. Gandharvas, gods, sages, nagas and kinnars rejoiced that their troubles were ending. Millions of fierce monkey warriors gnashed their teeth and rushed on, singing the glory of mighty Ram, Lord of Kosal.

label: छंद 2
hi: सहि सक न भार उदार अहिपति बार बारहिं मोहई।
गह दसन पुनि पुनि कमठ पृष्ट कठोर सो किमि सोहई॥
रघुबीर रुचिर प्रयान प्रस्थिति जानि परम सुहावनी।
जनु कमठ खर्पर सर्पराज सो लिखत अबिचल पावनी॥2॥
en: Sahi sak na bhaar udaar ahipati baar baarahin mohaee |
Gah dasan puni puni kamath prisht kathor so kimi sohaee ||
Raghubeer ruchir prayaan prasthiti jaani param suhaavanee |
Janu kamath kharpar sarparaaj so likhat abichal paavanee || 2 ||
mean: Even great Shesh could not bear the weight and kept faltering, gripping the tortoise's hard shell with his teeth again and again - as if, knowing Ram's march to be so glorious, he were engraving its holy story on the tortoise's back.

label: दोहा 35
hi: एहि बिधि जाइ कृपानिधि उतरे सागर तीर।
जहँ तहँ लागे खान फल भालु बिपुल कपि बीर॥
en: Ehi bidhi jaai kripaanidhi utare saagar teer |
Jahan tahan laage khaan phal bhaalu bipul kapi beer ||
mean: Thus the ocean of mercy reached the seashore and camped there; the many bear and monkey warriors began eating fruits here and there.

hi: जब ते जारि गयउ कपि लंका॥
en: Jab te jaari gayau kapi lankaa ||
mean: Over there the demons lived in fear ever since the monkey burned Lanka and left.

hi: निज निज गृहँ सब करहिं बिचारा।
en: Nij nij grihan sab karahin bichaaraa |
mean: In every house they thought: 'There is no escape for the demon race.'

hi: जासु दूत बल बरनि न जाई।
en: Jaasu doot bal barani na jaaee |
mean: 'His messenger's strength is beyond words - what good can come to the city when he himself arrives?'
Hearing from her maids what the townspeople said, Mandodari grew very anxious.

hi: रहसि जोरि कर पति पग लागी।
en: Rahasi jori kar pati pag laagee |
mean: In private, with joined palms, she touched her husband's feet and spoke words full of wisdom:

hi: मोर कहा अति हित हियँ धरहु॥
en: Mor kahaa ati hit hiyan dharahu ||
mean: 'My lord, give up your quarrel with Hari; take my well-meant advice to heart.'
'Merely remembering what his messenger did, the demon women miscarry.'
'Call your ministers and send his wife back, my lord, if you want your own good.'
'Sita has come like a winter night to the lotus grove of your clan.'

hi: हित न तुम्हार संभु अज कीन्हें॥
en: Hit na tumhaar sambhu aj keenhen ||
mean: 'Listen, lord: unless you return Sita, not even Shiva and Brahma can protect you.'

label: दोहा 36
hi: राम बान अहि गन सरिस निकर निसाचर भेक।
जब लगि ग्रसत न तब लगि जतनु करहु तजि टेक॥
en: Raam baan ahi gan saris nikar nisaachar bhek |
Jab lagi grasat na tab lagi jatanu karahu taji tek ||
mean: 'Ram's arrows are like a host of serpents and the demons like frogs. Before they are swallowed, give up your stubbornness and do something.'

hi: श्रवन सुनी सठ ता करि बानी।
en: Shravan sunee sath taa kari baanee |
mean: Hearing her words, the fool known everywhere for his pride laughed:

hi: मंगल महुँ भय मन अति काचा॥
en: Mangal mahun bhay man ati kaachaa ||
mean: 'It is true that women are timid by nature; even in good times their minds are full of fear.'
'If the monkey army comes, the poor demons will have something to eat.'
'The guardians of the worlds tremble in fear of me - how funny that my wife is afraid!'

hi: अस कहि बिहसि ताहि उर लाई।
en: As kahi bihasi taahi ur laaee |
mean: Saying this, he laughed, embraced her, and went to his court with even greater attachment.
Mandodari worried: 'Fate has turned against my husband.'
As he sat in court, news came: 'The whole army has crossed to the seashore.'

hi: ते सब हँसे मष्ट करि रहहू॥
en: Te sab hanse masht kari rahahoo ||
mean: He asked his ministers for advice; they all laughed: 'Be at ease.'
'You conquered gods and demons with no effort; what are men and monkeys to you?'

label: दोहा 37
hi: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस।
राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास॥
en: Sachiv baid gur teeni jaun priy bolahin bhay aas |
Raaj dharm tan teeni kar hoi begiheen naas ||
mean: If minister, physician and guru speak only pleasing words out of fear or hope, then kingdom, health and dharma are quickly destroyed.
So it was with Ravan: his counsellors only praised him to his face.
Seeing his chance, Vibhishan came and bowed his head at his brother's feet.

hi: पुनि सिरु नाइ बैठ निज आसन।
en: Puni siru naai baith nij aasan |
mean: Bowing again, he sat in his seat and, given leave, spoke:
'Kind brother, since you ask my view, I will advise you as well as I can.'

hi: सुजसु सुमति सुभ गति सुख नाना॥
en: Sujasu sumati subh gati sukh naanaa ||
mean: 'One who wants his own welfare - good fame, good sense, a good end and every happiness...'

hi: तजउ चउथि के चंद कि नाई॥
en: Tajau chauthi ke chand ki naaee ||
mean: '...should shun another man's wife, master, as one avoids the moon of the fourth night.'
'Even a lord of all fourteen worlds cannot last if he harms living beings.'

hi: अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ॥
en: Alap lobh bhal kahai na kooo ||
mean: 'A man may be an ocean of virtue and cultured, but if he has even a little greed, no one speaks well of him.'

label: दोहा 38
hi: काम क्रोध मद लोभ सब नाथ नरक के पंथ।
सब परिहरि रघुबीरहि भजहु भजहिं जेहि संत॥
en: Kaam krodh mad lobh sab naath narak ke panth |
Sab parihari raghubeerahi bhajahu bhajahin jehi sant ||
mean: 'Lust, anger, pride and greed are all paths to hell, lord. Give them all up and worship Ram, whom the saints worship.'
'Brother, Ram is no mere human king; he is lord of the worlds, Death even to Death.'
'He is Brahman - flawless, unborn, the Lord, all-pervading, unconquerable, without beginning or end.'
'Friend of cows, Brahmins, the earth and the gods, the ocean of mercy has taken a human body.'
'He delights his devotees and destroys the hordes of the wicked; he protects the Vedas and dharma, brother.'
'Give up enmity and bow to him; Ram removes the distress of all who bow to him.'
'Lord, give Sita back to him, and worship Ram, who loves without reason.'

hi: सरन गएँ प्रभु ताहु न त्यागा।
बिस्व द्रोह कृत अघ जेहि लागा॥
en: Saran gaen prabhu taahu na tyaagaa |
Bisv droh krit agh jehi laagaa ||
mean: 'The Lord does not abandon even one guilty of harming the world, once he seeks refuge.'

hi: सोइ प्रभु प्रगट समुझु जियँ रावन॥
en: Soi prabhu pragat samujhu jiyan raavan ||
mean: 'He whose name destroys the three kinds of suffering - know, Ravan, that this very Lord has appeared.'

label: दोहा 39 (क)
hi: बार बार पद लागउँ बिनय करउँ दससीस।
परिहरि मान मोह मद भजहु कोसलाधीस॥
en: Baar baar pad laagaun binay karaun dasasees |
Parihari maan moh mad bhajahu kosalaadhees ||
mean: 'Again and again I touch your feet and plead, ten-headed one: give up pride, delusion and arrogance, and worship the Lord of Kosal.'

label: दोहा 39 (ख)
hi: मुनि पुलस्ति निज सिष्य सन कहि पठई यह बात।
तुरत सो मैं प्रभु सन कही पाइ सुअवसरु तात॥
en: Muni pulasti nij sishy san kahi pathaee yah baat |
Turat so main prabhu san kahee paai suavasaru taat ||
mean: 'Sage Pulastya sent this message through his disciple; finding a good moment, I have told it to you at once, brother.'

hi: तासु बचन सुनि अति सुख माना॥
en: Taasu bachan suni ati sukh maanaa ||
mean: Malyavan, a very wise minister, was very pleased to hear these words.

hi: सो उर धरहु जो कहत बिभीषन॥
en: So ur dharahu jo kahat bibheeshan ||
mean: 'Son, your younger brother is an ornament of wisdom; take to heart what Vibhishan says.'

hi: दूरि न करहु इहाँ हइ कोऊ॥
en: Doori na karahu ihaan hai kooo ||
mean: Ravan said, 'These two fools praise the enemy. Will no one drive them away?'
Malyavan went home; Vibhishan, with joined palms, spoke again:

hi: सुमति कुमति सब कें उर रहहीं।
en: Sumati kumati sab ken ur rahaheen |
mean: 'Good sense and bad sense live in every heart, lord; so say the Puranas and Vedas.'
'Where there is good sense there is every prosperity; where there is bad sense, ruin follows.'
'Perverse bad sense has settled in your heart, so you take friend for foe and harm for good.'
'You have deep love for Sita, who is the night of doom for the demon race.'

label: दोहा 40
hi: तात चरन गहि मागउँ राखहु मोर दुलार।
सीत देहु राम कहुँ अहित न होइ तुम्हार॥
en: Taat charan gahi maagaun raakhahu mor dulaar |
Seet dehu raam kahun ahit na hoi tumhaar ||
mean: 'Brother, I hold your feet and beg you to honour my affection: give Sita back to Ram, and no harm will come to you.'
Vibhishan spoke wise counsel, in line with the learned, the Puranas and the Vedas.

hi: खल तोहि निकट मुत्यु अब आई॥
en: Khal tohi nikat mutyu ab aaee ||
mean: Hearing it, Ravan rose in anger: 'Wretch, your death is near now!'

hi: रिपु कर पच्छ मूढ़ तोहि भावा॥
en: Ripu kar pachchh moodh tohi bhaavaa ||
mean: 'Fool, you have always lived because I let you live, and now you favour the enemy.'

hi: कहसि न खल अस को जग माहीं।
भुज बल जाहि जिता मैं नाही॥
en: Kahasi na khal as ko jag maaheen |
Bhuj bal jaahi jitaa main naahee ||
mean: 'Tell me, wretch, who in the world have I not conquered by the strength of my arms?'

hi: मम पुर बसि तपसिन्ह पर प्रीती।
सठ मिलु जाइ तिन्हहि कहु नीती॥
en: Mam pur basi tapasinh par preetee |
Sath milu jaai tinhahi kahu neetee ||
mean: 'You live in my city and love the ascetics. Fool, go join them and preach to them.'
Saying this, he kicked him; still his younger brother clasped his feet again and again.
(Shiva says:) Uma, this is the greatness of a saint: he does good even to one who does him harm.

hi: तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा।
en: Tumh pitu saris bhalehin mohi maaraa |
mean: Vibhishan said, 'You are like a father to me; you were right to strike me. But your welfare lies in worshipping Ram.'

hi: सचिव संग लै नभ पथ गयऊ।
en: Sachiv sang lai nabh path gayaoo |
mean: Taking his ministers with him, he went through the sky, announcing to all:

label: दोहा 41
hi: रामु सत्यसंकल्प प्रभु सभा कालबस तोरि।
मै रघुबीर सरन अब जाउँ देहु जनि खोरि॥
en: Raamu satyasankalp prabhu sabhaa kaalabas tori |
Mai raghubeer saran ab jaaun dehu jani khori ||
mean: 'Ram's resolve is always true, and your court is in Death's grip. I now go to take refuge in Ram - do not blame me.'
The moment Vibhishan left, they all became doomed.
(Shiva says:) Bhavani, insulting a saint at once destroys all one's good fortune.
The moment Ravan cast out Vibhishan, the unfortunate one lost all his glory.
Vibhishan went joyfully toward Ram, his mind full of hopes:
'I will go and see his lotus feet, rosy and soft, which bring joy to his servants...'
'...the feet whose touch saved the sage's wife, which made the Dandak forest holy...'
'...the feet Sita held to her heart, which ran after the false deer...'

hi: हर उर सर सरोज पद जेई।
en: Har ur sar saroj pad jeee |
mean: '...the lotus feet in the lake of Shiva's heart - how fortunate I am to see them!'

label: दोहा 42
hi: जिन्ह पायन्ह के पादुकन्हि भरतु रहे मन लाइ।
ते पद आजु बिलोकिहउँ इन्ह नयनन्हि अब जाइ॥
en: Jinh paayanh ke paadukanhi bharatu rahe man laai |
Te pad aaju bilokihaun inh nayananhi ab jaai ||
mean: 'The feet whose sandals Bharat keeps his mind fixed on - today I will see them with these eyes.'
Thinking such loving thoughts, he quickly reached this shore of the ocean.
The monkeys saw Vibhishan coming and took him to be some special envoy of the enemy.
Stopping him there, they went to Sugriv and told him everything.
Sugriv said, 'Listen, Lord: Ravan's brother has come to meet you.'
The Lord said, 'Friend, what do you think?' Sugriv said, 'Listen, king of men:'
'Demons' tricks cannot be known; this shape-shifter has come for some purpose.'
'The fool has come to learn our secrets. I think we should keep him bound.'
Ram said, 'Friend, you have judged policy well; but my vow is to remove the fear of those who seek refuge.'
Hearing the Lord's words, Hanuman rejoiced: the Lord loves those who seek refuge.

label: दोहा 43
hi: सरनागत कहुँ जे तजहिं निज अनहित अनुमानि।
ते नर पावँर पापमय तिन्हहि बिलोकत हानि॥
en: Saranaagat kahun je tajahin nij anahit anumaani |
Te nar paavanr paapamay tinhahi bilokat haani ||
mean: 'Those who turn away one seeking refuge, fearing harm to themselves, are lowly and sinful; even seeing them is harmful.'
'Even one guilty of killing countless Brahmins, if he comes for refuge, I do not abandon.'
'The moment a soul turns toward me, the sins of countless births are destroyed.'

hi: भजनु मोर तेहि भाव न काऊ॥
en: Bhajanu mor tehi bhaav na kaaoo ||
mean: 'It is the nature of the sinful never to like worshipping me.'
'If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me at all?'

hi: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा।
मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥
en: Nirmal man jan so mohi paavaa |
Mohi kapat chhal chhidr na bhaavaa ||
mean: 'Only one with a pure mind reaches me; I do not like deceit, trickery or faults.'

hi: तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा॥
en: Tabahun na kachhu bhay haani kapeesaa ||
mean: 'Even if Ravan sent him to spy, Sugriv, there is no fear or loss in it.'
'Friend, Lakshman can kill all the demons in the world in a moment.'
'And if he has come for refuge in fear, I will guard him like my own life.'

label: दोहा 44
hi: उभय भाँति तेहि आनहु हँसि कह कृपानिकेत।
जय कृपाल कहि चले अंगद हनू समेत॥
en: Ubhay bhaanti tehi aanahu hansi kah kripaaniket |
Jay kripaal kahi chale angad hanoo samet ||
mean: 'Either way, bring him here,' said the abode of mercy, smiling. Saying 'Victory to the merciful one!', Sugriv went with Angad and Hanuman.
Respectfully placing Vibhishan in front, the monkeys went to where compassionate Ram was.
From afar Vibhishan saw the two brothers, who give joy to the eyes.
Then, seeing Ram, abode of beauty, he stopped short, gazing without blinking.
Long arms, eyes like red lotuses, a dark body - he who frees from fear those who bow to him.
Lion-like shoulders, a broad chest, and a face that would charm countless Kamadevs.

hi: मन धरि धीर कही मृदु बाता॥
en: Man dhari dheer kahee mridu baataa ||
mean: Eyes full of tears, body thrilling, he steadied himself and spoke gently:
'Lord, I am Ravan's brother, born in the demon race, O protector of the gods.'
'I have a dark nature that loves sin, as the owl loves darkness.'

label: दोहा 45
hi: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर।
त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर॥
en: Shravan sujasu suni aayaun prabhu bhanjan bhav bheer |
Traahi traahi aarati haran saran sukhad raghubeer ||
mean: 'Hearing your glory, I have come, Lord who removes the fear of worldly existence. Save me, save me, remover of suffering, Ram who gives joy to those seeking refuge!'
When the Lord saw him prostrate after saying this, he rose at once with great joy.

hi: दीन बचन सुनि प्रभु मन भावा।
en: Deen bachan suni prabhu man bhaavaa |
mean: Pleased by his humble words, the Lord took him in his long arms and held him to his heart.
With his brother he embraced him, seated him close, and spoke - he who removes his devotees' fear:
'Tell me, king of Lanka, are you and your family well? You live in a bad place.'
'You live day and night among the wicked; how do you keep to dharma, friend?'

hi: अति नय निपुन न भाव अनीती॥
en: Ati nay nipun na bhaav aneetee ||
mean: 'I know all your ways; you are very wise and dislike wrongdoing.'

hi: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता।
en: Baru bhal baas narak kar taataa |
mean: 'Better to live in hell, friend, than may Providence give the company of the wicked.'

hi: जौं तुम्ह कीन्ह जानि जन दाया॥
en: Jaun tumh keenh jaani jan daayaa ||
mean: Vibhishan said, 'Seeing your feet, Lord, now I am well, since you have shown kindness, knowing me as your own.'

label: दोहा 46
hi: तब लगि कुसल न जीव कहुँ सपनेहुँ मन बिश्राम।
जब लगि भजत न राम कहुँ सोक धाम तजि काम॥
en: Tab lagi kusal na jeev kahun sapanehun man bishraam |
Jab lagi bhajat na raam kahun sok dhaam taji kaam ||
mean: 'No soul is well, nor finds peace of mind even in dreams, until it gives up desire, the home of sorrow, and worships Ram.'

hi: तब लगि हृदयँ बसत खल नाना।
en: Tab lagi hridayan basat khal naanaa |
mean: 'Until then many villains live in the heart - greed, delusion, envy, arrogance and pride...'

hi: जब लगि उर न बसत रघुनाथा।
en: Jab lagi ur na basat raghunaathaa |
mean: '...as long as Ram, with bow and arrows and quiver at his waist, does not dwell in the heart.'
'Attachment is a dark night, pleasant to the owls of liking and aversion...'

hi: तब लगि बसति जीव मन माहीं।
जब लगि प्रभु प्रताप रबि नाहीं॥
en: Tab lagi basati jeev man maaheen |
Jab lagi prabhu prataap rabi naaheen ||
mean: '...and it stays in the mind only until the sun of the Lord's glory rises.'

hi: अब मैं कुसल मिटे भय भारे।
en: Ab main kusal mite bhay bhaare |
mean: 'Now I am well and my great fears are gone, Ram, seeing your lotus feet.'

hi: ताहि न ब्याप त्रिबिध भव सूला॥
en: Taahi na byaap tribidh bhav soolaa ||
mean: 'Merciful one, those you favour are not touched by the threefold pain of worldly life.'
'I am a demon of very low nature and have never done a good deed.'

hi: जासु रूप मुनि ध्यान न आवा।
तेहिं प्रभु हरषि हृदयँ मोहि लावा॥
en: Jaasu roop muni dhyaan na aavaa |
Tehin prabhu harashi hridayan mohi laavaa ||
mean: 'Yet the Lord whose form even sages cannot hold in meditation has joyfully held me to his heart.'

label: दोहा 47
hi: अहोभाग्य मम अमित अति राम कृपा सुख पुंज।
देखेउँ नयन बिरंचि सिब सेब्य जुगल पद कंज॥
en: Ahobhaagy mam amit ati raam kripaa sukh punj |
Dekheun nayan biranchi sib seby jugal pad kanj ||
mean: 'How immensely fortunate I am! Ram, home of grace and joy, with my own eyes I have seen the lotus feet served by Brahma and Shiva.'
Ram said: 'Listen, friend, I tell you my nature, which Bhushundi, Shiva and Parvati know.'
'Even if a man is an enemy of all creation, when he comes in fear seeking my refuge...'

hi: तजि मद मोह कपट छल नाना।
en: Taji mad moh kapat chhal naanaa |
mean: '...and gives up pride, delusion, deceit and trickery, I at once make him like a saint.'
'Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, home, friends and family -'

hi: मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥
en: Mam pad manahi baandh bari doree ||
mean: 'gathering the threads of attachment to all of these, he twists them into a rope that binds his mind to my feet.'

hi: हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं॥
en: Harash sok bhay nahin man maaheen ||
mean: 'He sees all alike, has no desires, and feels no joy, grief or fear in his mind.'

hi: अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें।
en: As sajjan mam ur bas kaisen |
mean: 'Such a good soul lives in my heart as wealth lives in a miser's heart.'
'Saints like you are dear to me; for no other reason do I take a body.'

label: दोहा 48
hi: सगुन उपासक परहित निरत नीति दृढ़ नेम।
ते नर प्रान समान मम जिन्ह कें द्विज पद प्रेम॥
en: Sagun upaasak parahit nirat neeti dridh nem |
Te nar praan samaan mam jinh ken dvij pad prem ||
mean: 'Those who worship God with form, delight in others' good, are firm in right conduct and love the feet of the learned are as dear to me as life.'
'Listen, king of Lanka: you have all these virtues, so you are extremely dear to me.'
Hearing Ram's words, all the monkey troops cried, 'Victory to the treasury of grace!'
Hearing the Lord's words, Vibhishan could not have enough of that nectar for the ears.
He clasped the Lord's lotus feet again and again; his boundless love could not be contained.
'Listen, Lord, master of all moving and unmoving beings, protector of those who bow, knower of every heart:'

hi: प्रभु पद प्रीति सरित सो बही॥
en: Prabhu pad preeti sarit so bahee ||
mean: 'At first some desire remained in my heart, but it has been swept away by the river of love for your feet.'
'Now, merciful one, grant me your purifying devotion, which is ever dear to Shiva's heart.'
Saying 'So be it,' the steadfast Lord at once asked for seawater.
'Friend, though you have no desire for it, seeing me never goes without fruit in this world.'

hi: अस कहि राम तिलक तेहि सारा।
en: As kahi raam tilak tehi saaraa |
mean: Saying this, Ram anointed him with the royal mark; endless flowers rained from the sky.

label: दोहा 49 (क)
hi: रावन क्रोध अनल निज स्वास समीर प्रचंड।
जरत बिभीषनु राखेउ दीन्हेहु राजु अखंड॥
en: Raavan krodh anal nij svaas sameer prachand |
Jarat bibheeshanu raakheu deenhehu raaju akhand ||
mean: Vibhishan, burning in the fire of Ravan's anger fanned by his own fierce breath, was saved by Ram and given an undivided kingdom.

label: दोहा 49 (ख)
hi: जो संपति सिव रावनहि दीन्हि दिएँ दस माथ।
सोइ संपदा बिभीषनहि सकुचि दीन्ह रघुनाथ॥
en: Jo sampati siv raavanahi deenhi dien das maath |
Soi sampadaa bibheeshanahi sakuchi deenh raghunaath ||
mean: The wealth Shiva gave Ravan after he offered his ten heads - Ram gave that same fortune to Vibhishan, and even felt shy at giving so little.

hi: अस प्रभु छाड़ि भजहिं जे आना।
ते नर पसु बिनु पूँछ बिषाना॥
en: As prabhu chhaadi bhajahin je aanaa |
Te nar pasu binu poonchh bishaanaa ||
mean: Those who leave such a Lord to worship another are beasts without tail or horns.

hi: प्रभु सुभाव कपि कुल मन भावा॥
en: Prabhu subhaav kapi kul man bhaavaa ||
mean: Knowing Vibhishan as his own, Ram accepted him; the Lord's nature delighted the monkeys.
Then the all-knowing one, who lives in every heart, who is all forms yet beyond all and detached...
...upholder of right conduct, who took human form to destroy the demon race, spoke:
'Listen, Sugriv and brave king of Lanka: how shall we cross this deep ocean?'
'It teems with crocodiles, serpents and fish, and is fathomless and hard to cross in every way.'
Vibhishan said, 'Listen, Lord: your arrow could dry up countless oceans.'
'Even so, good conduct says one should first go and request the ocean.'

label: दोहा 50
hi: प्रभु तुम्हार कुलगुर जलधि कहिहि उपाय बिचारि।
बिनु प्रयास सागर तरिहि सकल भालु कपि धारि॥
en: Prabhu tumhaar kulagur jaladhi kahihi upaay bichaari |
Binu prayaas saagar tarihi sakal bhaalu kapi dhaari ||
mean: 'Lord, the ocean is an elder of your clan; he will think of a way, and the whole army of bears and monkeys will cross without effort.'
Ram said, 'Friend, you suggest a good way; let us do it, if Providence helps.'

hi: मंत्र न यह लछिमन मन भावा।
राम बचन सुनि अति दुख पावा॥
en: Mantr na yah lachhiman man bhaavaa |
Raam bachan suni ati dukh paavaa ||
mean: This advice did not please Lakshman; hearing Ram's words, he was much troubled.
'Lord, what reliance is there on fate? Grow angry and dry up the ocean.'
'Fate is the only prop of a coward; it is the lazy who cry "fate, fate".'
Hearing this, Ram laughed and said, 'We will do just that - be patient.'
Calming his brother thus, the Lord went to the seashore.
First he bowed his head in salutation, then sat on the shore on a mat of kusha grass.
As soon as Vibhishan had come to the Lord, Ravan sent spies after him.

label: दोहा 51
hi: सकल चरित तिन्ह देखे धरें कपट कपि देह।
प्रभु गुन हृदयँ सराहहिं सरनागत पर नेह॥
en: Sakal charit tinh dekhe dharen kapat kapi deh |
Prabhu gun hridayan saraahahin saranaagat par neh ||
mean: Disguised as monkeys, they saw everything, and in their hearts praised the Lord's virtues and his love for those who seek refuge.
They began openly praising Ram's nature, forgetting their disguise in their love.

hi: रिपु के दूत कपिन्ह तब जाने।
en: Ripu ke doot kapinh tab jaane |
mean: Then the monkeys knew them as enemy spies, bound them all and brought them to Sugriv.
Sugriv said, 'Listen, monkeys: maim the demons and send them back.'
Hearing Sugriv, the monkeys rushed and paraded them, bound, through the whole camp.
The monkeys began beating them in many ways; though they cried piteously, they did not stop.
The spies cried, 'Whoever cuts off our noses and ears is sworn by the Lord of Kosal!'
Hearing this, Lakshman called them close and, moved by pity, smiled and freed them at once.
'Give this letter to Ravan: "Read Lakshman's words, destroyer of your clan."'

label: दोहा 52
hi: कहेहु मुखागर मूढ़ सन मम संदेसु उदार।
सीता देइ मिलेहु न त आवा काल तुम्हार॥
en: Kahehu mukhaagar moodh san mam sandesu udaar |
Seetaa dei milehu na ta aavaa kaal tumhaar ||
mean: 'And tell that fool my generous message by word of mouth: return Sita and come to terms, or your death has come.'
Bowing at Lakshman's feet, the spies left at once, recounting Ram's virtues.
Singing Ram's glory, they reached Lanka and bowed at Ravan's feet.
Ravan laughed and asked, 'Shuk, why don't you tell me how you are?'
'Then give me news of Vibhishan, whose death has come so near.'
'The fool left Lanka where he ruled; the wretch will be crushed like a worm.'
'And tell me of the army of bears and monkeys, driven here by cruel fate...'
'...whose lives are protected only by the soft-hearted ocean.'

hi: जिन्ह के हृदयँ त्रास अति मोरी॥
en: Jinh ke hridayan traas ati moree ||
mean: 'Then tell me of those ascetics, whose hearts are full of fear of me.'

label: दोहा 53
hi: की भइ भेंट कि फिरि गए श्रवन सुजसु सुनि मोर।
कहसि न रिपु दल तेज बल बहुत चकित चित तोर॥
en: Kee bhai bhent ki phiri gae shravan sujasu suni mor |
Kahasi na ripu dal tej bal bahut chakit chit tor ||
mean: 'Did you meet them, or did they turn back on hearing of my fame? Why don't you speak of the enemy's might? Your mind seems quite amazed.'
Shuk said, 'Lord, as you kindly asked, so accept what I say, setting aside anger.'
'When your brother went and met him, Ram at once anointed him king.'
'Hearing we were Ravan's spies, the monkeys bound us and gave us much pain.'
'They began to cut our ears and noses; when we swore by Ram, they let us go.'

hi: बदन कोटि सत बरनि न जाई॥
en: Badan koti sat barani na jaaee ||
mean: 'Lord, you ask about Ram's army - it could not be described with a billion mouths.'
'Bears and monkeys of many colours, fierce-faced, huge and terrifying.'

hi: जेहिं पुर दहेउ हतेउ सुत तोरा।
सकल कपिन्ह महँ तेहि बलु थोरा॥
en: Jehin pur daheu hateu sut toraa |
Sakal kapinh mahan tehi balu thoraa ||
mean: 'The one who burned the city and killed your son is the weakest of all the monkeys.'
'There are countless named warriors, fierce and terrible, each with the strength of countless elephants.'

label: दोहा 54
hi: द्विबिद मयंद नील नल अंगद गद बिकटासि।
दधिमुख केहरि निसठ सठ जामवंत बलरासि॥
en: Dvibid mayand neel nal angad gad bikataasi |
Dadhimukh kehari nisath sath jaamavant balaraasi ||
mean: 'Dvivid, Mayand, Neel, Nal, Angad, Gad, Vikatasya, Dadhimukh, Kesari, Nishath, Shath, and Jambavan, a mass of strength.'

hi: इन्ह सम कोटिन्ह गनइ को नाना॥
en: Inh sam kotinh ganai ko naanaa ||
mean: 'All these monkeys are equal to Sugriv, and who can count the millions like them?'
'By Ram's grace their strength is matchless; they count the three worlds as straw.'
'I have heard, ten-headed one, that there are eighteen padmas of monkey commanders.'

hi: नाथ कटक महँ सो कपि नाहीं।
जो न तुम्हहि जीतै रन माहीं॥
en: Naath katak mahan so kapi naaheen |
Jo na tumhahi jeetai ran maaheen ||
mean: 'Lord, there is no monkey in that army who could not defeat you in battle.'
'In great anger they wring their hands, but Ram gives no order.'

hi: पूरहीं न त भरि कुधर बिसाला॥
en: Pooraheen na ta bhari kudhar bisaalaa ||
mean: 'They say, "We will dry up the ocean with its fish and serpents, or else fill it with great mountains."'
'"We will grind Ravan into dust" - such are the words of all the monkeys.'
'They roar and threaten, naturally fearless, as if they would swallow Lanka.'

label: दोहा 55
hi: सहज सूर कपि भालु सब पुनि सिर पर प्रभु राम।
रावन काल कोटि कहु जीति सकहिं संग्राम॥
en: Sahaj soor kapi bhaalu sab puni sir par prabhu raam |
Raavan kaal koti kahu jeeti sakahin sangraam ||
