mean: 'The bears and monkeys are brave by nature, and above them is Lord Ram. They could defeat millions of Deaths in battle, let alone Ravan.'

hi: सेष सहस सत सकहिं न गाई॥
en: Sesh sahas sat sakahin na gaaee ||
mean: 'Ram's splendour, strength and wisdom could not be sung even by a hundred thousand Sheshas.'

hi: सक सर एक सोषि सत सागर।
en: Sak sar ek soshi sat saagar |
mean: 'He could dry a hundred oceans with one arrow, yet, wise in conduct, he asked your brother's advice.'
'On his advice he is asking the ocean for a path, with mercy in his heart.'

hi: जौं असि मति सहाय कृत कीसा॥
en: Jaun asi mati sahaay krit keesaa ||
mean: Hearing this, Ravan laughed: 'With such sense, no wonder he made monkeys his allies!'
'Trusting the words of a born coward, he has begun begging the ocean like a stubborn child.'

hi: रिपु बल बुद्धि थाह मैं पाई॥
en: Ripu bal buddhi thaah main paaee ||
mean: 'Fool, why praise them falsely? I have measured the enemy's strength and wisdom.'
'One whose adviser is the timid Vibhishan - where in the world can he find victory and glory?'

hi: सुनि खल बचन दूत रिस बाढ़ी।
en: Suni khal bachan doot ris baadhee |
mean: Hearing the wicked one's words, the spy grew angry and, seeing the moment, took out the letter.
'Ram's brother gave this letter. Have it read, lord, and soothe your heart.'
Ravan laughed, took it in his left hand, called a minister and had it read out.

label: दोहा 56 (क)
hi: बातन्ह मनहि रिझाइ सठ जनि घालसि कुल खीस।
राम बिरोध न उबरसि सरन बिष्नु अज ईस॥
en: Baatanh manahi rijhaai sath jani ghaalasi kul khees |
Raam birodh na ubarasi saran bishnu aj ees ||
mean: 'Fool, do not destroy your clan by pleasing your mind with talk. Opposing Ram, you will not be saved even by taking refuge with Vishnu, Brahma or Shiva.'

label: दोहा 56 (ख)
hi: की तजि मान अनुज इव प्रभु पद पंकज भृंग।
होहि कि राम सरानल खल कुल सहित पतंग॥
en: Kee taji maan anuj iv prabhu pad pankaj bhring |
Hohi ki raam saraanal khal kul sahit patang ||
mean: 'Either give up pride and, like your brother, become a bee at the Lord's lotus feet, or be a moth, with your wicked clan, in the fire of Ram's arrows.'
Afraid at heart but smiling outwardly, Ravan announced to all:
'Lying on the ground, he grasps at the sky - this little ascetic's boasting!'

hi: कह सुक नाथ सत्य सब बानी।
en: Kah suk naath saty sab baanee |
mean: Shuk said, 'Lord, every word is true. Give up your proud nature and understand.'
'Hear my words without anger: Lord, give up your enmity with Ram.'
'Ram's nature is very gentle, though he is king of all the worlds.'

hi: मिलत कृपा तुम्ह पर प्रभु करिही।
en: Milat kripaa tumh par prabhu karihee |
mean: 'When you meet him, he will show you mercy and hold not a single offence against you.'
'Give Janaki back to Ram. Lord, do just this much that I ask.'
When he said 'give back Vaidehi', the wicked one kicked him.

hi: नाइ चरन सिरु चला सो तहाँ।
en: Naai charan siru chalaa so tahaan |
mean: Bowing at his feet, Shuk went to where Ram, ocean of mercy, was.
Bowing, he told his story, and by Ram's grace regained his true state.
(Shiva says:) Bhavani, he had been a wise sage, turned into a demon by sage Agastya's curse.

hi: मुनि निज आश्रम कहुँ पगु धारा॥
en: Muni nij aashram kahun pagu dhaaraa ||
mean: Bowing again and again at Ram's feet, the sage returned to his hermitage.

label: दोहा 57
hi: बिनय न मानत जलधि जड़ गए तीन दिन बीति।
बोले राम सकोप तब भय बिनु होइ न प्रीति॥
en: Binay na maanat jaladhi jad gae teen din beeti |
Bole raam sakop tab bhay binu hoi na preeti ||
mean: Three days passed and the dull ocean did not heed the request. Then Ram said in anger, 'Without fear there is no friendship.'
'Lakshman, bring my bow and arrows; I will dry up the ocean with fiery arrows.'

hi: सठ सन बिनय कुटिल सन प्रीती।
en: Sath san binay kutil san preetee |
mean: 'Pleading with a fool, friendship with the crooked, good counsel to the miserly...'
'...talk of wisdom to one lost in attachment, praise of detachment to the very greedy...'
'...calm to the angry, Hari's story to the lustful - these are like sowing seeds in barren land.'

hi: यह मत लछिमन के मन भावा॥
en: Yah mat lachhiman ke man bhaavaa ||
mean: Saying this, Ram strung his bow; this pleased Lakshman.
The Lord fitted a fierce arrow; a blaze arose within the ocean's heart.
Crocodiles, serpents and fish were distressed; when the ocean felt its creatures burning...

hi: कनक थार भरि मनि गन नाना।
en: Kanak thaar bhari mani gan naanaa |
mean: ...it gave up its pride and came in a Brahmin's form, with a golden platter full of jewels.

label: दोहा 58
hi: काटेहिं पइ कदरी फरइ कोटि जतन कोउ सींच।
बिनय न मान खगेस सुनु डाटेहिं पइ नव नीच॥
en: Kaatehin pai kadaree pharai koti jatan kou seench |
Binay na maan khages sunu daatehin pai nav neech ||
mean: (Kakbhushundi says:) Listen, Garud: a banana tree bears fruit only when cut, however much one waters it; the lowly do not heed requests, they bend only when rebuked.

hi: सभय सिंधु गहि पद प्रभु केरे।
en: Sabhay sindhu gahi pad prabhu kere |
mean: In fear, the ocean clasped the Lord's feet: 'Forgive all my faults, Lord.'

hi: इन्ह कइ नाथ सहज जड़ करनी॥
en: Inh kai naath sahaj jad karanee ||
mean: 'Sky, wind, fire, water and earth - their nature is to be inert, Lord.'
'They were created by Maya at your will, for the sake of creation, as all scriptures say.'

hi: प्रभु आयसु जेहि कहँ जस अहई।
सो तेहि भाँति रहे सुख लहई॥
en: Prabhu aayasu jehi kahan jas ahaee |
So tehi bhaanti rahe sukh lahaee ||
mean: 'Each lives happily in the way the Lord has ordained for it.'

hi: प्रभु भल कीन्ही मोहि सिख दीन्ही।
en: Prabhu bhal keenhee mohi sikh deenhee |
mean: 'Lord, you did well to teach me a lesson, though my bounds were also set by you.'
'The drum, the unlettered, the shudra, the animal and the woman are all fit for "taadna".' (The ocean speaks; this word and line are read very differently by different commentators.)
'By the Lord's might I would dry up and the army would cross, but that brings me no honour.'

hi: करौं सो बेगि जौ तुम्हहि सोहाई॥
en: Karaun so begi jau tumhahi sohaaee ||
mean: 'The scriptures say the Lord's command cannot be disobeyed; I will quickly do whatever pleases you.'

label: दोहा 59
hi: सुनत बिनीत बचन अति कह कृपाल मुसुकाइ।
जेहि बिधि उतरै कपि कटकु तात सो कहहु उपाइ॥
en: Sunat bineet bachan ati kah kripaal musukaai |
Jehi bidhi utarai kapi kataku taat so kahahu upaai ||
mean: Hearing these humble words, the merciful one smiled and said, 'Friend, tell us how the monkey army can cross.'

hi: नाथ नील नल कपि द्वौ भाई।
en: Naath neel nal kapi dvau bhaaee |
mean: The ocean said, 'Lord, the two monkey brothers Neel and Nal received a sage's blessing in childhood.'

hi: तिन्ह कें परस किएँ गिरि भारे।
en: Tinh ken paras kien giri bhaare |
mean: 'By their touch, even heavy rocks will float on the sea through your glory.'

hi: मैं पुनि उर धरि प्रभु प्रभुताई।
en: Main puni ur dhari prabhu prabhutaaee |
mean: 'And I, holding the Lord's greatness in my heart, will help as much as I can.'

hi: जेहिं यह सुजसु लोक तिहुँ गाइअ॥
en: Jehin yah sujasu lok tihun gaaia ||
mean: 'In this way, Lord, have the ocean bridged, so that this glory is sung in the three worlds.'

hi: एहि सर मम उत्तर तट बासी।
हतहु नाथ खल नर अघ रासी॥
en: Ehi sar mam uttar tat baasee |
Hatahu naath khal nar agh raasee ||
mean: 'With this arrow, Lord, slay the wicked men full of sin who live on my northern shore.'
Hearing this, the merciful Ram, steadfast in battle, at once removed the ocean's pain.
Seeing Ram's great strength and valour, the ocean was delighted and relieved.
He told the Lord everything, bowed at his feet and departed.

label: छंद 1
hi: निज भवन गवनेउ सिंधु श्रीरघुपतिहि यह मत भायऊ।
यह चरित कलि मलहर जथामति दास तुलसी गायऊ॥
सुख भवन संसय समन दवन बिषाद रघुपति गुन गना।
तजि सकल आस भरोस गावहि सुनहि संतत सठ मना॥
en: Nij bhavan gavaneu sindhu shreeraghupatihi yah mat bhaayaoo |
Yah charit kali malahar jathaamati daas tulasee gaayaoo ||
Sukh bhavan sansay saman davan bishaad raghupati gun ganaa |
Taji sakal aas bharos gaavahi sunahi santat sath manaa ||
mean: The ocean went to his home; Ram liked his counsel. Tulsidas has sung this story, which removes the impurity of Kali, as well as he could. Ram's virtues are a home of joy, dispel doubt and destroy sorrow - so, foolish mind, give up every other hope and reliance and always sing and hear them.

label: दोहा 60
hi: सकल सुमंगल दायक रघुनायक गुन गान।
सादर सुनहिं ते तरहिं भव सिंधु बिना जलजान॥
en: Sakal sumangal daayak raghunaayak gun gaan |
Saadar sunahin te tarahin bhav sindhu binaa jalajaan ||
mean: Singing the virtues of Ram, Lord of Raghus, gives every blessing. Those who hear them with reverence cross the ocean of worldly life without any boat.

label: इति
mean: Thus ends the fifth step (Sunderkand) of the holy Ramcharitmanas, which destroys all the impurities of the Kali age.
Perform the aarti of dear Hanuman, destroyer of the wicked, a manifestation of Ram's power.

hi: रोग दोष जाके निकट न झाँके॥
en: Rog dosh jaake nikat na jhaanke ||
mean: By whose strength great mountains tremble, and near whom disease and evil dare not come.
Son of Anjani, giver of great strength, ever the helper of saints.
Ram sent him with the task in hand; he burned Lanka and brought news of Sita.

hi: लंका सो कोट समुद्र सी खाई।
en: Lankaa so kot samudr see khaaee |
mean: Lanka's fortress had a moat like the sea, yet the son of the Wind crossed it without delay.
He burned Lanka, destroyed the demons, and fulfilled the work of Sita and Ram.
When Lakshman lay unconscious, he brought the Sanjivani herb by dawn and saved his life.
Entering the netherworld and breaking Yama's bonds, he tore off Ahiravan's arms.
With his left arm he slew the demon hosts; with his right he saved the saints.
Gods, men and sages perform his aarti, crying 'Jai, jai, jai Hanuman!'
On a golden platter the camphor flame glows; Mother Anjana performs the aarti.
Whoever sings Hanuman's aarti dwells in Vaikunth and attains the highest state.
Ram destroyed Lanka; Tulsidas sang the Lord's glory.

label: टेक
hi: कीरति कलित ललित सिय पी की॥
en: Keerati kalit lalit siy pee kee ||
mean: Aarti to the holy Ramayan, the beautiful, graceful glory of Sita's beloved.
Brahma and the gods, the sages and Narad sing it; so does Valmiki, master of wisdom. Shuk, Sanak and the others, Shesh and Saraswati, and Hanuman - all describe its fine glory.

hi: छओ सास्त्र सब ग्रंथन को रस॥
मुनि जन धन संतन को सरबस।
en: Chhao saastr sab granthan ko ras ||
Muni jan dhan santan ko sarabas |
mean: The Vedas and eighteen Puranas sing it; it is the essence of the six philosophies and all scriptures. It is the wealth of sages, everything to the saints, and its essence is accepted by all.
Shiva and Bhavani sing it always, as does the wise sage Agastya. Vyas and the best of poets have praised it, and Kakbhushundi and Garud too.

hi: दलन रोग भव मूरि अमी की।
तात मात सब बिधि तुलसी की॥
en: Dalan rog bhav moori amee kee |
Taat maat sab bidhi tulasee kee ||
mean: It removes the impurity of Kali and makes worldly pleasures tasteless; it is the beautiful adornment of the maiden Liberation. It is the nectar-root that destroys the disease of worldly life - father and mother in every way to Tulsidas.
